properties.summary: A lava flow dated at about 1.2 million years forms Mutsurejima island just off the SW tip of Honshu (Nakano et al., 2001-). Kifune volcano (1.6 or 1.3 million years old), 7 km E, consists of basaltic scoria cones and lava flows.

properties.name: Shikuma
properties.summary: Shikuma volcano consists of Shikumaga-take (dated at about 450,000 years ago) and Dake-yama lava domes (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Tokuyama-Mitake
properties.summary: Tokuyama-Mitake is a lava dome in SW Honshu dated at about 0.43 million years (Nakano et al., 2001-).  It is also known as Mitake-yama or Kinpo-san.

properties.name: Sengoku
properties.summary: The Sengoku volcano group consists of a group of four mid-Pleistocene lava domes active from about 0.5 to 0.36 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Chojagahara
properties.summary: Chojagahara is a 1.7 million year old pyroclastic cone and lava flow (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Aonoyama
properties.summary: The Aonoyama volcano group consists of about 10 lava domes from about 1.3 to 0.15 million years in age (Nakano et al., 2001-). The volcanic products have a narrow chemical composition similar to that of Daisen and consist of biotite and hornblende andesites that often contain granulitic inclusions (Matsuhisa and Kurasawa, 1983).

properties.name: Oetakayama
properties.summary: Oetakeyama consists of a group of lava domes active from about 1.8 to 0.8 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-). Kano and Takarada (2007) noted late-Pliocene to early Pleistocene activity, including at the early Pleistocene Senyama pyroclastic cone north of the Oetakayama (O'e-Takayama). The latest activity noted was K-Ar dated at about 1.8-1.6 million years.

properties.name: Yokote
properties.summary: The Yokote volcano group was active between about 2.3 and 0.9 million years and consists of 10 monogenetic volcanoes (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Noro
properties.summary: The Noro basaltic lava flow was erupted about 1.1 million years ago from a monogenetic volcano (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Daikonjima
properties.summary: A scoria cone and lava flow at Daikonjima was erupted about 250,000 or 200,000 years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Tsuruta
properties.summary: The Tsuruta volcano group consists of a group of scoria cones about 1.2 million years in age aligned NW-SE, including the Takatsuka-yama cone (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Daisen
properties.summary: Daisen volcano, along the northern coast of SW Honshu, has been the source of large explosive eruptions during the late Pleistocene. The last dated major eruption took place about 17,000-18,000 years before present, but at least one large tephra deposit is younger (Machida and Arai, 1992).

properties.name: Ogino-Sen
properties.summary: The Ogino-Sen volcano group in eastern Tottori Prefecture consists of 20 monogenetic volcanoes from 1.2 to 0.4 million years in age (Nakano et al., 2001-).  The adjacent Mikata volcano group in western Hyogo Prefecture consists of 8 monogenetic volcanoes from 1.7 to 0.22 million years in age.

properties.name: Kannabe
properties.summary: The Kannabe volcano group is the westernmost and youngest of a cluster of monogenetic volcanoes that are part of the Kita-Tajima volcano group in Hyogo Prefecture, along with Mesaka, Kamisano, and Gembudo volcanoes.  A radiocarbon age of 19,000 years before present was obtained from the small shield volcano of Kannabe-yama (Ono et al., 1981), and Nakano et al (2001-) listed an age of 20,000 or 10,000 years.

properties.name: Takara
properties.summary: Takara-yama (also known as Takura-yama) is a small shield volcano topped by a pyroclastic cone and was active about 0.4 or 0.3 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).  It is the SE-most volcano of the Kita-Tajima volcano group in SW Honshu.

properties.name: Nanzaki
properties.summary: Nanzaki (also known as Ikenohara) is a basaltic pyroclastic cone at the southern tip of the Izu Peninsula dated at about 450,000 or 400,000 years (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Jaishi
properties.summary: Jaishiyama is a small andesitic shield volcano with a lava flow dated at about 1.4-1.3 million years (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Tanaba
properties.summary: Tanaba-yama is an andesitic stratovolcano dated at about 1.5-1.2 million years (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Daruma
properties.summary: Daruma-yama is an andesitic stratovolcano dated at about 0.8-0.5 million years (Nakano et al., 2001-).  Ida volcano and the underlying Osezaki volcano lie to the north at the NW tip of the Izu Peninsula.

properties.name: Tenshi
properties.summary: Tenshi is an andesitic and dacitic stratovolcano dated at about 1.7-1.4 million years (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Usami
properties.summary: Usami is a basaltic-to-andesitic stratovolcano north of the Izu-Toba volcano group dated at about 0.9 to 0.4 million years (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Taga
properties.summary: Taga is an basaltic-to-andesitic stratovolcano SW of Atami City dated at about 0.7-0.3 million years (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Yugawara
properties.summary: Yugawara is an andesitic and basaltic stratovolcano south of Hakone volcano dated at about 0.4-0.2 million years (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Ashitaka
properties.summary: Ashitaka-yama is a large basaltic-to-dacitic stratovolcano and lava dome SE of Fuji that was active from about 0.4-0.1 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Kirigamine
properties.summary: Kirigamine is a small shield volcano and lava dome (Wada-Toge) that lies west of Kita-Yatsugatake volcano  and NW of Yatsugatake volcano.  Kirigamine was active about 1.3-0.75 million years ago (Oikawa and Nishiki, 2005).

properties.name: Utsukushigahara
properties.summary: Utsukushigahara, NE of Yatstuga-take, was active about 1.6-1.2 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Ueno
properties.summary: Ueno volcano is a small basaltic-to-andesitic shield volcano and lava flow that was active about 1.6 or 1.5 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).  Ono et al. (1981) listed a Potassium-Argon date of <110,000 thousand years ago.

properties.name: Yuga-mine
properties.summary: Yuga-mine is a rhyolitic lava dome SW of On-take volcano that was active about 0.1 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Kurofuji
properties.summary: The Kurofuji (Black Fuji) lava-dome complex and Kanaga-take and Kayaga-take stratovolcanoes active from about 1 million to 0.4 or 0.2 million years ago lie in Chichibu-Tama National Park north of the city of Kofu (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Yatsugatake
properties.summary: The older Yatsugatake volcano was active about 1 million years ago and the younger was active about 0.2 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001). This complex of N-S-trending stratovolcanoes extends for about 10 km and is also known as Minami Yatsugatake ("Southern Eight Peaks") (Matsuhisa and Kurasawa, 1983).

properties.name: Eboshi-Washigatake
properties.summary: Eboshi and Washigatake are early Pleistocene andesitic stratovolcanoes active about 1.6-1.1 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Bishamondake
properties.summary: Bishamondake is an andesitic stratovolcano active about 0.4-0.25 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Dainichigatake
properties.summary: Dainichigatake is an andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcano that was active about 1.1-0.9 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Ryohaku Maruyama
properties.summary: Ryohaku Maruyama (named to distinguish from Maruyama volcano in Hokkaido) is an andesitic stratovolcano active about 0.4-0.3 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Gankyoji
properties.summary: Gankyoji-yama is a Pliocene-Pleistocene andesitic stratovolcano active until about 1.3 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Kyogatake
properties.summary: The Kyogatake volcano group consists of andesitic stratovolcanoes active about 1.4-0.7 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Dainichiyama
properties.summary: Dainichiyama is an early Pleistocene andesitic stratovolcano west of Haku-san volcano (Ono et al., 1981). This volcano was not listed by Nakano et al. (2001-).

properties.name: Tomuro
properties.summary: The Tomuro lava-dome complex contains four domes that were active from about 0.4-0.3 million years (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Kamitakara
properties.summary: Kamitakara (or Takara) volcano was the source of deposits forming the Kamitakara pyroclastic flow plateau.  The dacitic-to-rhyolitic deposits were erupted about 0.75 or 0.70 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).  Ono et al. (1981) listed a Potassium-Argon date of  about 600,000 years.

properties.name: Kaminoroka
properties.summary: Kaminoroka volcano produced andesitic and dacitic lava flows about 0.4-0.2 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Hodakadake
properties.summary: Hodakadake, the highest of a rugged group of peaks in the scenic Northern Alps National Park, lies within the Hodaka Graben, the source of two major explosive eruptions about 1.75 million years ago. The eruption of the caldera-forming Nyukawa Pyroclastic Flow Deposit about 1.76 million years ago (Kimura and Nagahashi, 2007) was followed by the Ebisutoge-Fukuda Tephra, with an estimated volume of 380-490 km3 (Kataoka et al., 2001).

properties.name: Momisawadake
properties.summary: Momisawadake volcano in the Northern Japan Alps was the source of a dacitic-rhyolitic pyroclastic-flow plateau. The complex includes the Sueindani vent and the Okuhida pyroclastic-flow deposit and was active sometime between about 0.65 and 0.3 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Shirouma-Oike
properties.summary: The andesitic and dacitic Shirouma-Oike volcanic complex consists of the Norikura-dake stratovolcano and the Kazafuki-dake lava dome.  An older volcano was active 0.8-0.5 million years ago and younger volcano was active since 0.2 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Madarao
properties.summary: Madarao-yama is an andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcano and lava domes that were active about 0.7-0.55 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001).

properties.name: Kurohime
properties.summary: Kurohime is a stratovolcano and associated lava domes south of Myoko volcano that were active from about 250,000 to 50,000 years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Iizuna
properties.summary: Iizuna stratovolcano south of Kurohime volcano was active about 0.34-0.15 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Motodori
properties.summary: The andesitic Motodori-yama lava dome was active about 0.2 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Minakami
properties.summary: Minakami-yama lava dome was active about 0.3 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-) and is a post-caldera dome of Matsushiro volcano.

properties.name: Eboshi
properties.summary: The Eboshi volcano group immediately west of Asama volcano includes a group of andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcanoes and lava domes that were active about 0.97-0.35 million years ago (Takahashi and Miyake, 2004; Takahashi, 2004).

properties.name: Hanamagari
properties.summary: The andesitic Hanamagari-yama and neighboring Asamakakushi-yama stratovolcanoes immediately east of Asama volcano were active about 1.1-0.7 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Azumayasan
properties.summary: Azumayasan is an andesitic stratovolcano and lava dome that was active about 0.9-0.3 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-). A plinian eruption took place about 0.3 million years ago.

properties.name: Omeshidake
properties.summary: The andesitic Omeshidake stratovolcano west of Kusatsu-Shirane volcano was active about 1.1 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Takayashiro
properties.summary: Takayashiro-yama is an andesitic stratovolcano that was active about 0.3-0.2 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Sekita
properties.summary: The andesitic Sekita volcano was active about 1.7-1.1 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Kenashi
properties.summary: Kenashi-yama is an andesitic stratovolcano active about 1.6-1.0 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Torikabuto
properties.summary: The andesitic Torikabuto-yama stratovolcano was active about 0.9-0.7 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Naeba
properties.summary: The andesitic Naeba-san stratovolcano and caldera was active about 0.8-0.2 Ma (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Iiji
properties.summary: The andesitic Iiji-san stratovolcano was active about 0.3-0.2 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).  The Iiji Moka Pumice was erupted about 0.22-0.23 million years ago.

properties.name: Masugata
properties.summary: The andesitic Masugata-yama pyroclastic cone and lava flow was active about 1.1 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Komochi-Onoko
properties.summary: The Komochi-Onoko volcano group NW of Maebashi City consists of the andesitic Komochi-yama stratovolcano and lava dome on the east and andesitic Onoko-yama stratovolcano on the west.  Komochi-yama was active from about 0.9-0.2 million years and Onoko-yama from about 1.3-1.2 million years (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Kinunuma-Nenakusa
properties.summary: The dacitic Kinunuma volcano produced a lava flow and pyroclastic flow about 0.24 or 0.20 million years ago. The Kinunuma-Kurodahara tephra consists of pumice fall deposits (~5 km3) and mostly-welded pyroclastic flow deposits (less than 1 km3), erupted at 0.20-0.24 Ma. Andesitic and dacitic lava domes of the Nenakusa-yama volcano to the SE were active about 0.3 million years ago.

properties.name: Sukai-Kesemaru
properties.summary: The basaltic-to-dacitic Sukai stratovolcano was active about 1.6-0.9 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).  Koshin-zan volcano is part of the Sukai edifice, and activity of the roughly 1-million-year-old Kesemaru-yama volcano to the south overlapped with activity at Sukai-san volcano.

properties.name: Numanokami
properties.summary: The andesitic Numanokami-yama stratovolcano was active about 1.1 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Hotaka
properties.summary: The andesitic-to-dacitic Hotaka-yama volcano (also known as Joshu-Hotaka) was active about 1.2-1 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Ayame-daira
properties.summary: The Ayame-daira stratovolcano south of Ozegahara in Nikko National Park was active about 1.6 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).  Nikura-yama volcano lies to the SE.

properties.name: Nyoho-Akanagi
properties.summary: Nyoho and Akanagi volcano consists of a basaltic-to-dacitic stratovolcano and lava dome active about 0.5-0.4 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Sunagohara
properties.summary: The rhyolitic Sunagohara caldera and lava dome, east of Numazawa caldera, was active about 0.29-0.22 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).  The Sunagohara-Kubota tephra is made up of pumice fall deposits (ca. 4 km3 in volume) and pyroclastic flow deposits (more than 2 km3 in volume), erupted from Sunagohara caldera at about 0.22Ma.

properties.name: Nekoma
properties.summary: The andesitic Nekoma volcano, immediately W of Bandai, was active about 1-0.8 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-). The caldera is about 3 km in diameter and contains a lake on the western side.

properties.name: Futamata
properties.summary: Futamata-yama is a late Pleistocene (about 140,000 or 90,000 years old) stratovolcano and lava dome (Nakano et al., 2001-). A thick lava flow extends to the NW. It is located within the Quaternary Tonohetsuri caldera (Yamamoto, 1995; 2007). The oval-shaped Narioka caldera cuts the western rim of Tonohetsuri caldera and the western rim of the older Ono caldera.

properties.name: Aizu Nunobiki
properties.summary: Aizu Nunobiki-yama is an andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcano that was active about 1.4 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Asakusa
properties.summary: Asakusa-dake is an andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcano active about 1.7-1.5 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Sumon
properties.summary: Sumon volcano is an andesitic stratovolcano active about 2.4-1.7 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).  The main part of the edifice of Sumon-dake was constructed during the early Quaternary.

properties.name: Aoso
properties.summary: Aoso volcano is an andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcano at the SE end of the Zao massif.  Aoso-yama was active about 0.4-0.3 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).  Aoso was constructed within a Pleistocene caldera.

properties.name: Mukaimachi
properties.summary: Mukaimachi is a dacitic and andesitic caldera with a post-caldera lava dome.  Post-caldera activity at Mukaimachi took place about 0.8-0.6 million years ago Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Shirataka
properties.summary: Shirataka is an andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcano NW of the Zao volcanic massif. Shiratakayama was active about 0.9-0.7 million years ago. Growth of a stratovolcano was followed by emplacement of a pyroclastic flow and growth of lava domes. Late-stage collapse produced a large debris avalanche and formed a 4-km-wide breached crater.

properties.name: Ganto-Kamuro
properties.summary: Ganto and Kamuro volcanoes form the Kita-Zao (North Zao) volcano group.  They were active about 0.4-0.3 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Adachi
properties.summary: Adachi is a dacitic pyroclastic cone that was the source of the Adachi-Medeshima pumice deposit about 80,000 years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Daito
properties.summary: Daito volcano is an andesitic stratovolcano NNE of the Zao volcanic massif. Daito-dake was active about 1 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Funagata
properties.summary: The Funagata volcanic complex consists of two basaltic-to-andesitic stratovolcanoes NW of Sendai City.  Funagata-yama was active about 0.9-0.5 million years ago and Izumiga-take volcano about 1.5-1.1 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Gassan
properties.summary: Gassan is a massive andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcano south of Chokai volcano that was active about 900,000-300,000 years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).  It was constructed with a large Pleistocene caldera.

properties.name: Onikobe
properties.summary: Onikobe caldera, located SW of Kurikoma volcano, is one of the few calderas in Japan with evidence of ring fractures and a resurgent dome.  The Takahinata lava dome was last active about 350,000 years ago according to a fission-track date.  Onikobe was active until about 0.2 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).   Geysers were said to be discovered about 1700 years ago at Onikobe, and geysers and hot springs are present today within the caldera.

properties.name: Takamatsu
properties.summary: Takamatsu volcano (Takamatsu-dake) is a dacitic stratovolcano active about 0.3 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).  Takamatsu was constructed within a Pliocene caldera.

properties.name: Kobinai
properties.summary: Kobanai volcano (Kobinai-yama) is an andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcano active about 1-0.6 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Yakeishi
properties.summary: Yakeishi volcano (Yakeishi-dake) is an andesitic stratovolcano that was active about 1-0.2 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Tazawa
properties.summary: Tazawa was considered to be a late-Pleistocene caldera (Japan Assoc. Quat. Res. 1987), however Nakano et al. (2001-) noted that it is uncertain whether the depression was formed by volcanic activity.  The elevation listed is that of the surface of Tazawa lake.

properties.name: Kayo
properties.summary: Early or mid-Pleistocene (Japan Assoc. Quat. Res., 1987).

properties.name: Nyuto-Takakura
properties.summary: The Nyuto-Takakura volcano group consists of Nyuto-san, Takakura-yama, Hiragakura-yama, Marumori, Sankagu-yama, Sasamori-yama, Yumori-yama volcanoes.  The basaltic-to-dacitic volcano group was active about 0.6-0.1 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Tamagawa
properties.summary: The dacitic and rhyolitic Tamagawa caldera was the source of the Tamagawa Ignimbrite associated with formation of a pre-Yaka-yama caldera.  The caldera was active about 2 million and 1 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Nanashigure
properties.summary: Nanashigure volcano is a Pleistocene pyroclastic-flow plateau and lava dome.   Nanashigure-yama was active about 1.1-0.9 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Daira-Komagatake
properties.summary: Daira-Komagatake is an andesitic stratovolcano active about 0.2 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Tashiro
properties.summary: Tashiro-dake is an andesitic stratovolcano and lava dome that is younger than about 0.6 million years (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Moriyoshi
properties.summary: Moriyoshi-zan is a basaltic-to-dacitic stratovolcano and lava dome that was active about 1.1-0.7 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Kanpu
properties.summary: The small Kanpu stratovolcano lies on the Oga Peninsula along the western coast of Honshu NW of Akita City. It was at one time considered to be Holocene, but later work has shown it to be late Pleistocene. Accounts of radiocarbon dates of about 2,700 years BP for a pumice eruption followed by a pyroclastic flow (Hasenaka et al., 1992) have been revised, and the report on the 1810 "eruption" submitted to the Shognate was created by the people of the Akita C…

properties.name: Okiura
properties.summary: The 15-km-wide Okiura caldera was formed by the eruption of the Aoni Tuff about 1.5 million years ago.  Post-caldera volcanoes comprise several lava domes including Kenashi-yama.

properties.name: Mutsu-Hiuchidake
properties.summary: Mutsu-Hiuchidake, on the Shimokita Peninsula, is the northernmost volcano on the island of Honshu. The andesitic-dacitic stratovolcano is Pleistocene in age, with dated activity during an interval ranging from about 700,000 to 50,000 years ago, although fumarolic activity continues.

properties.name: Udonejima
properties.summary: Udonejima, though technically part of the Izu Volcanic Arc, is actually considered to be situated just behind the true volcanic front, along a line of volcanoes that is oblique to the Izu Trench. The volcanic rocks of this lineament are characterized by high-alumina basalts, calc-alkaline basalts, andesites, and rhyolites (Onuma et al., 1983).

properties.name: Onoharajima
properties.summary: Onoharajima is considered to be situated behind the true front of the Izu Volcanic Arc, along a line of volcanoes that is oblique to the Izu Trench. The volcanic rocks of this lineament are characterized by high-alumina basalts, calc-alkaline basalts, andesites, and rhyolites (Onuma et al., 1983). Onoharajima is dominated by andesites of calc-alkaline composition (Onuma et al., 1983).

properties.name: Tracey Seamount
properties.summary: The conical Tracey Seamount, ~50 km W of the northern end of Guam, had pumice dredged from the summit (Corwin, 1971).

properties.name: Shikaribetsu Group
properties.summary: Shikaribetsu consists of a group of andesitic-to-dacitic lava domes west and south of Lake Shikaribetsu in central Hokkaido. The youngest domes were constructed along a ENE-WSW line south of the lake. The largest dome, Higashi-Nupukaushinupuri, was built at the SW, breached end of a horseshoe-shaped crater. Two or more large debris-avalanche deposits extend to the south.

properties.name: Esan Maruyama
properties.summary: Esan Maruyama, an andesitic stratovolcano lying NW of E-san volcano, was active about 0.2 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Yokotsu
properties.summary: Most of Yokotsu-dake volcano formed during the Pliocene, but Nakitsura-yama on the east side was probably constructed during the late Quaternary (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Oshima-Kojima
properties.summary: Oshima-Kojima, also known as Matsumae-Kojima, is an andesitic stratovolcano whose summit forms a small island off the SW tip of Hokkaido (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Oshima Maruyama
properties.summary: Oshima Maruyama, a Pleistocene stratovolcano and lava dome near the SW tip of Hokkaido, was active from about 2.5-1.5 million years ago.

properties.name: Hakodateyama
properties.summary: Hakodateyama, a low dacitic stratovolcano, rises above the city of Hakodate in SW Hokkaido.

properties.name: Zenikame
properties.summary: A 2-km-wide shallow submarine caldera just off the SW tip of Hokkaido, SE of Hakodate City reaches to within 30 m of the ocean surface. It was the source of the Zenikame-Menagawa (Z-M) tephra about 33,000-45,000 years ago.

properties.name: Nigorikawa
properties.summary: The Mori geothermal field is located in the late-Pleistocene Nigorikawa caldera in SW Hokkaido. The small 3-km-wide caldera along the shores of Uchiura Bay WNW of Komagatake volcano, was formed during a major explosive eruption about 12,000 years ago. The caldera-forming eruption included the emplacement of pyroclastic-fall and -surge deposits and pyroclastic-flow deposits that extend north and west to the Pacific coast.

properties.name: Okushiri-Katsumayama
properties.summary: Okushiri-Katsumayama volcano lies at the northern end of Okushiri Island off the SW coast of Hokkaido and consists of three centers, Horonaigawa caldera, Katsumayama and Nishi-Katsumayama. They were active about 0.7-0.2 million years ago (Kano et al., 2006).

properties.name: Kariba
properties.summary: Kariba-yama, an andesitic stratovolcano along the SW coast of Hokkaido, was active about 0.8-0.25 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Washibetsu
properties.summary: Washibetsu-dake volcano, an andesitic stratovolcano SE of Usu volcano, was active about 0.5 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Akaigawa
properties.summary: Akaigawa, a  late-Pliocene double caldera containing several somma volcanoes, was active about 1.7-1.3 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Shiribetsu
properties.summary: Shiribetsu volcano, located immediately SE of Yotei volcano in southwestern Hokkaido, is a small, 1107-m-high andesitic stratovolcano that contains a 1.5-km-wide crater breached widely to the west.  It was created by a massive debris avalanche that removed the summit and swept more than 7 km to the west, forming a hummocky deposit at the SE foot of Yotei volcano.

properties.name: Orofure-Raiba
properties.summary: The Orofure-Raibe volcano group consists of Orofure-yama and Raibe-dake andesitic stratovolcanoes lying immediately west of Kuttara volcano.  They were active about 0.6 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Horohoro-Tokushumbetsu
properties.summary: The andesitic Horohoro-yama and Tokushumbetsu volcanoes were active about 0.7 or 0.6 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Raiden
properties.summary: The Raiden-yama volcano complex along the SW coast of Hokkaido consists of  Raiden-yama, Iwanai-dake and Mekunnai-dake volcanoes and was active about 1.4-0.8 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Soranuma
properties.summary: Soranuma, a small andesitic shield volcano and lava flow, was active about 0.8 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Sapporo
properties.summary: Sapporo volcano (Sapporo-dake), a small andesitic shield volcano and lava flow, was active about 0.8 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Tomuraushi Volcanic Group
properties.summary: The andesitic-to-dacitic Tomuraushi) volcano group located between Tokachi and Daisetsu volcanoes consists of a half dozen stratovolcanoes and lava domes that were active about 1.1-0.1 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Chubetsu
properties.summary: Chubetsu volcano (Chubetsu-dake or Tyubetu-dake), an andesitic stratovolcano SE of Daisetsu volcano, was active about 1-0.8 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Tokachi-Eboshi
properties.summary: The Tokachi-Eboshi volcano group consists of several lava domes and volcanic necks that were active about 1.8-0.7 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Niseikaushuppe
properties.summary: The basaltic Niseikaushuppe-dake stratovolcano was active about 1.1 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Tengu-Hirayama
properties.summary: The Tengu-Hirayama volcano group consists of the andesitic-to-dacitic Tengu and Hira-yama volcanoes.  They were active about 1.3-1.0 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).  Ariake-yama and Hirami-yama form the high points of Tengu and Hira-yama volcanoes, respectively.  The northern part of this area contains the 1.6-1.3 million year Kitamitoge volcanic rocks.

properties.name: Shiitokoro
properties.summary: Shiitokoro-yama, an andesitic-to-dacitic lava dome and lava flow, was active about 1.4 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Kumaneshiri
properties.summary: Kumaneshiri volcano consists of two andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcanoes, Nishi-Kumaneshiri-dake and Kumaneshiri-dake, that were active about 1.3 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Tokachi-Mitsumata
properties.summary: Tokachi-Mitsumata, a rhyolitic caldera that was the source of the Muka and Meto pyroclastic flows, was active about 0.6-0.3 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).  Ishii et al. (2008) listed dates of around 1 million years ago for formation of the Tokachi-Mitsumata caldera.

properties.name: Birao
properties.summary: The Birao volcano group consists of Birao-yama and Sattomonai andesitic-to-rhyolitic stratovolcanoes.  Birao was active about 500,000-300,000 years ago and Sattomonai volcano about 100,000 years ago (Nakano et al, 2001-).

properties.name: Samakkenupuri
properties.summary: Samakkenupuri volcano consists of the andesitic Samakkenupuri-yama and Shibetsu-dake stratovolcanoes that were active about 1.1-0.8 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Musa
properties.summary: The andesitic-to-dacitic Musa-dake volcano was active about 0.9-0.5 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Shari
properties.summary: The andesitic-to-dacitic Shari-dake volcano was active about 0.3-0.25 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Unabetsu
properties.summary: The basaltic-to-andesitic Unabetsu-dake stratovolcano was active about 0.9-0.5 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Onnebetsu
properties.summary: Onnebetsu volcano was active about 0.4-0.2 million years ago and Chinishibetsu volcano about 0.2-0.1 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).

properties.name: Shiretoko
properties.summary: Shiretoko volcano, the NE-most in Hokkaido, was active about 0.6-0.2 million years ago (Nakano et al., 2001-).  The andesitic Shiretoko-dake volcano lies at the tip of the Shiretoko Peninsula.

properties.name: Moekeshiwan [Lvinaya Past]
properties.summary: The rim of the 7 x 9 km Moekeshiwan [Lvinaya Past] caldera on southern Iturup Island drops to 50 m below sea level on the NW side. Lvinaya Past, meaning Lion's Jaw, derives from a rock formation resembling a sleeping lion. The caldera is breached on the NW, where a shallow 5-km-wide passage opens to the Sea of Okhotsk. The caldera floor is about 550 m below sea level and lies almost 1 km below the caldera rim.

properties.name: Kuril Arc at 45.0°N
properties.summary: Designated as "Volcano 8.10" in a catalog of submarine Kuril Arc volcanic centers (Avdeiko, 1992), this seamount is located ~22 km NNW of the Iturup Island peninsula with Etorofu-Atosanupuri stratovolcano. Although Gushchenko (1979) listed a submarine eruption in 1967 based on an oral communication from Gushkov, the description is more consistent with hydrothermal activity and dredging of nearby volcanic material. Blokh et al.

properties.name: Rucharu [Golets-Tornyi Group]
properties.summary: Rucharu, with the small cones of Golets and Tornyi, is SW of Moyorodake (Medvezhia) volcano at one of the narrowest parts of Iturup Island, and formed during the late Pleistocene or early Holocene. A small lava flow from the Tornyi cone reportedly occupies a broad glacial cirque. The andesitic-dacitic Golets cone, constructed above the eroded remnants of the Pleistocene Parusnaya Mountain volcano, produced lava flows that reached the coast.

properties.name: Chirippusan [Chirip]
properties.summary: Chirippusan (also simply Chirip) volcano is on the Chirip Peninsula, which extends N into the Sea of Okhotsk from central Iturup Island. The summits of two overlapping stratovolcanoes are ~4.5 km apart along a volcanic ridge, with Kitachirippusan on the north and Minamichirippu (also called Bogdan Khmelnitskii) on the south. Lava flows from both edifices are truncated by a 4-km-wide depression on the west side of the peninsula.

properties.name: Rakkibetsudake [Demon]
properties.summary: Rakkibetsudake [Demon], along with the Pleistocene Kamui volcano, forms the northern peninsula of the NW end of Iturup Island. Gorshkov (1970) wrote that the large cone was built in the Holocene, with lavas that "flooded U-shaped valleys of the second glaciation" and late activity was "an eastward-directed explosion" followed by "subsequent erosion [that] cut a large canyon through from the caldera to the shore of Vries Strait." No subsequent work is known…

properties.name: Rudakov
properties.summary: The small Rudakov stratovolcano is on the NW side of the Tokotan Isthmus on the Sea of Okhotsk coast of central Urup Island. The basaltic andesite cone has a 500-m-diameter summit crater containing a 300-m-diameter lake. The age was considered to be late Pleistocene or early Holocene by Gorshkov (1970), but no later research is known that describes or dates eruption deposits.

properties.name: Tri Sestry
properties.summary: The Tri Sestry ("Three Sisters") volcanic complex is located in the center of Urup Island, in the south-central Kuril Islands. Erosion of this andesitic massif has cut deep ravines on the flanks and produced multiple peaks around a river valley open to the NNE. The southern range of those peaks is known as Petr Shmidt Ridge.

properties.name: Arkhangelsky
properties.summary: The Arkhangelsky volcanic massif, designated as "Volcano 6.12" in a catalog of submarine Kuril Arc volcanic centers (Avdeiko, 1992), is located in the Bussol Strait between Simushir and Urup Islands, E of Chirpoi. In their review of research on this volcano, Blokh et al.

properties.name: Urbich Caldera
properties.summary: The 6-km-wide Urbich caldera (also known as Urumombetsu), formed during a Pleistocene interglacial period and hosts a freshwater lake. No activity has occurred during the Holocene (Gorshkov, 1970). Urbich partially overlies the Rokko caldera.

properties.name: Tsirk
properties.summary: The 6-km-wide Tsirk caldera formed during the Pleistocene.  The caldera floor contains a hot lake (Gorshkov 1970).

properties.name: Brontona Island
properties.summary: Pleistocene according to Gorshkov (1970) map.

properties.name: Kuntomintar
properties.summary: Kuntomintar is a Pleistocene andesitic stratovolcano at the southern end of Shiashkotan Island in the central Kuriles. A central cone fills a 4-4.5 km caldera, whose rim is visible on the NE side. A second caldera on the west side is breached to the west. An Ainu village that reportedly was destroyed by an eruption in 1872 was later found to be located near Sinarka volcano (Gorshkov, 1970).

properties.name: Shestakov
properties.summary: Shestakov is an eroded volcanic complex in the north-central part of Onekotan Island, south of the Nemo Peak caldera system. Gorshkov (1970) notes that this "massif was formed in preglacial times and then underwent glacial abrasion and postglacial erosion to such a degree that at present it is extremely difficult to restore its original form." No age information is known for the Shestakov volcanics, but it was not included in Gorshkov (1958, CAVW) or the I…

properties.name: Makanru Island
properties.summary: Mapped as Pleistocene (Gorshkov 1970).

properties.name: Mashkovtsev
properties.summary: The small basaltic Mashkovtsev stratovolcano forms a peninsula on the Sea of Okhotsk near the southern tip of the Kamchatka Peninsula. It was considered Holocene by Masurenkov (1980), and there is a postglacial summit cone (Sviatlovsky 1959). Two basaltic cones are located to the north. This was not included by Ponomareva et al. (2007) in their review of Holocene volcanoes in Kamchatka.

properties.name: Kell
properties.summary: Kell volcano is a small stratovolcano considered to be Holocene by Masurenkov (1980), located within the Prizrak caldera immediately north of Zheltovsky volcano. This remote volcanic complex consists of three partially nested 3-5 km wide calderas containing lava domes and several small stratovolcanoes, the largest of which is Kell. This was not included by Ponomareva et al. (2007) in their review of Holocene volcanoes in Kamchatka.

properties.name: Belenkaya
properties.summary: Belenkaya is a small basaltic volcano considered to be Holocene by Masurenkov (1980) that lies SW of Ksudach and NW of Kell. The conical stratovolcano rises 700 m above a topographic low in the center of the southern Kamchatka Peninsula. This was not included by Ponomareva et al. (2007) in their review of Holocene volcanoes in Kamchatka.

properties.name: Piratkovsky
properties.summary: Piratkovsky, identified by Masurenkov (1980) as a mid-Pleistocene to Holocene stratovolcano with a small caldera, is  NE of Khodutka volcano. It partially overlaps Pleistocene volcanoes to the NW and lies at the eastern margin of the Quaternary volcanic chain of southern Kamchatka. This was not included by Ponomareva et al. (2007) in their review of Holocene volcanoes in Kamchatka.

properties.name: Ostanets
properties.summary: The Ostanets shield volcano, considered to be Holocene by Masurenkov (1980), is located south of the Pleistocene Savan volcano surrounded by a large group of late-Pleistocene to Holocene cinder cones. Small pyroclastic cone groups also occur north and east of Igolki volcano, ~30 km SW of Savan. This was not included by Ponomareva et al. (2007) in their review of Holocene volcanoes in Kamchatka.

properties.name: Otdelniy
properties.summary: The Otdelniy shield volcano, considered early Holocene by Masurenkov (1980), lies east of the Savan River, across from the Pleistocene Savan volcano. It, along with adjacent shield volcanoes and a large group of late-Pleistocene to Holocene basaltic pyroclastic cones, is about halfway between Khodutka and Opala volcanoes.

properties.name: Golaya
properties.summary: Golaya is a small basaltic stratovolcano of Pleistocene-to-Holocene age  (Masurenkov, 1980) south of Asacha volcano. It is elongated in a N-S direction and overlooks small shield volcanoes and cinder cones related to regional basaltic volcanism near the headwaters of the Asacha River. This was not included by Ponomareva et al. (2007) in their review of Holocene volcanoes in Kamchatka.

properties.name: Karymshina
properties.summary: The large 15 x 25 km early Pleistocene Karymshina caldera is located SW of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatskiy and N of Gorely volcano. It produced about 800 km3 of rhyolitic ignimbrite about 1.78 million years ago, followed by rhyolitic post-caldera extrusive material (Bindeman et al, 2019). There are about a dozen extrusive domes surrounding the structure. Reported K-Ar dates from the domes are in the 2.2-0.5 Ma range.

properties.name: Schmidt
properties.summary: Schmidt volcano is a large mid- to late-Pleistocene eroded shield-like volcano located N of Kronotsky volcano and SW of Gamchen (Lutchitsky, 1974). A dike complex is prominent along a NE-trending fault zone. Andreev et al. (1988) reported that following the cessation of Pleistocene activity, regional basaltic volcanism produced some monogenetic cinder cones on the E and NE flanks during the Holocene. However, Ponomareva et al.

properties.name: Maly Payalpan
properties.summary: Maly Payalpan (Little Payalpan) is a small Quaternary shield-like volcano NE of Ichinsky. Andesitic lava domes of uncertain age are located to the south. It is of basaltic andesite to andesitic composition and was constructed on top of a late-Pliocene to early Pleistocene alkaline basaltic plateau. Basaltic cinder cones of  late-Pleistocene to possible Holocene age are on the edifice.

properties.name: Bolshoi Payalpan
properties.summary: The Quaternary shield-like Bolshoi Payalpan (Big Payalpan) volcano is north of Ichinsky in the southern Sredinny Range. It is of dominantly basaltic andesite to andesitic composition and overlain by a late-Pleistocene to possible Holocene age basaltic cinder cones. The Pleistocene Payalpan shield volcano is located immediately SW of Bolshoi Payalpan, and itself has several lava flows of possible Holocene age that descend its NW and SE flanks.

properties.name: Plosky
properties.summary: The small Quaternary shield-like Plosky volcano south of the Bolshaya Kimitina River is SE of Ichinsky near the SE margin of the Sredinny Range. The summit consists of a small basaltic stratovolcano overtopping the lava shield. Early geological studies in the Sredinny Range (Ogorodov et al., 1972) assigned Holocene ages based on morphology, but later work noted that these volcanoes appear younger because they have less tephra cover than those in eastern Ka…

properties.name: Akhtang
properties.summary: The late Pleistocene Akhtang Massif is located between the Bolshaya Kimitina and Kozyrevka rivers SE of Ichinsky volcano in the southern Sredinny Range. This stratovolcano is at the NE end of line of smaller monogenetic cones extending about 16 km SE. Volynets et al. (2020) obtained K-Ar dates of about 250-310 ka from lava samples taken near the youngest cones at the SW end of the chain.

properties.name: Kozyrevsky
properties.summary: Kozyrevsky is a small Quaternary basaltic to basaltic andesite shield-like volcano located east of the Bystraya River, ~40 km E of Ichinsky in the southern Sredinny Range. It is topped by a small stratovolcano and has a large cinder cone on the SW flank.

properties.name: Romanovka
properties.summary: Romanovka is a small Quaternary stratovolcano immediately north of the Kozyrevka River in the southern Sredinny Range. A broad area of cinder cones and associated lava flows is present on both sides of the river and extends primarily to the east of the volcano to the SE margin of the Sredinny Range.

properties.name: Uksichan
properties.summary: The large gently dipping shield-like Uksichan volcano covers 1,850 km2, and is the largest of the Sredinny Range with a 300 km3 volume. Several dacitic domes fill the 12-km-wide central caldera; the largest of these rises 900 m above the caldera floor to form the summit. Initial lava flows traveled up to 15-20 km, but later flows were thicker and more viscous.

properties.name: Kulkev
properties.summary: Kulkev is a small Quaternary basaltic to basaltic andesite shield-like volcano in the southern Sredinny Range that is dwarfed by its massive neighbor immediately to the south, Uksichan.Early geological studies in the Sredinny Range (Ogorodov et al., 1972) assigned Holocene ages based on morphology, but later work noted that these volcanoes appear younger because they have less tephra cover than those in eastern Kamchatka.

properties.name: Geodesistov
properties.summary: Geodesistov is a small basaltic to basaltic andesite shield-like volcano immediately WNW of the larger Anaun in the southern Sredinny Range. A small cone with a lava flow was constructed to the WSW, and a small lava field is to the south.

properties.name: Anaun
properties.summary: Anaun is a Quaternary basaltic stratovolcano NE of Uksichan in the southern Sredinny Range. A chain of NE-SW-trending cinder cones extends to the SW, and another chain of numerous cinder cones displays the same orientation S and SE of the volcano.

properties.name: Krainy
properties.summary: Krainy is a small Quaternary basaltic to basaltic andesite shield-like volcano NE of Anaun in the southern Sredinny Range. Cinder cones are found across the flanks and a lava flow is on the SW. Early geological studies in the Sredinny Range (Ogorodov et al., 1972) assigned Holocene ages based on morphology, but later work noted that these volcanoes appear younger because they have less tephra cover than those in eastern Kamchatka.

properties.name: Kekurny
properties.summary: Kekurny is the northernmost of two overlapping small Quaternary basaltic to basaltic andesite shield-like volcanoes north of Anaun and west of Krainy volcanoes in the southern Sredinny Range. A chain of small cinder cones was constructed along a NE-SW-trending rift cutting across the volcano. The Bunanya shield immediately to the south has cinder cones on its NE flank.

properties.name: Eggella
properties.summary: Eggella is a small basaltic to basaltic andesite shield-like volcano on the flank of the Pleistocene Chavycha shield, west of the axis of the southern Sredinny Range. A chain of small cones on the E flank trends NE-SW. Early geological studies in the Sredinny Range (Ogorodov et al., 1972) assigned Holocene ages based on morphology, but later work noted that these volcanoes appear younger because they have less tephra cover than those in eastern Kamchatka.

properties.name: Verkhovoy
properties.summary: Verkhovoy, a small Quaternary basaltic to basaltic andesite shield-like volcano in the central Sredinny Range, is dwarfed by its massive neighbor to the NNE, Alney-Chashakondzha. Early geological studies in the Sredinny Range (Ogorodov et al., 1972) assigned Holocene ages based on morphology, but later work noted that these volcanoes appear younger because they have less tephra cover than those in eastern Kamchatka. Researchers such as Ponomareva et al.

properties.name: Cherny
properties.summary: Cherny is a small Quaternary stratovolcano immediately north of the massive Alney-Chashakondzha complex in the central Sredinny Range. An ENE-WSW-trending line of cinder cones was constructed on the western flank of Cherny, which is the southernmost of a cluster of small stratovolcanoes and shields trending NE from Alney-Chashakondzha.

properties.name: Pogranychny
properties.summary: Pogranychny is the highest and easternmost of a group of three small Quaternary basaltic to basaltic andesite shield-like volcanoes in the central Sredinny Range about 20 km NE of teh Alney-Chashakondzha complex. A chain of cinder cones extends NNE-SSW across Vodorazdelny at the N to Centralny at the SW.

properties.name: Zaozerny
properties.summary: A group of three small Quaternary basaltic to basaltic andesite shield-like volcanoes are present slightly east of the axis of the central Sredinny Range, about 30 km NE of Alney-Chashakondzha volcano and NNW of Lake Dvukhyurtochnoye.  The highest and westernmost is Zaozerny, with Oleny to the SE and Kastriulya volcano to the NE.

properties.name: Bliznets
properties.summary: Bliznets is a Quaternary basaltic stratovolcano on the crest of the central Sredinny Range SW of Kebeney volcano. Cinder cones were constructed on the E flank, and a group of cones and associated lava flows cover the northern side of the volcano.

properties.name: Kebeney
properties.summary: Kebeney is a prominent Quaternary basaltic to basaltic andesite shield-like volcano in the central Sredinny Range. Two groups of NE-SW-trending cinder cones are on the SW and SE flanks, and other cinder cones are on the NE flank. Lavas surround the small eroded Kalgnitunup cone to the SW.

properties.name: Fedotych
properties.summary: Fedotych, a small Quaternary basaltic to basaltic andesite shield-like volcano, is about 20 km E of the crest of the central Sredinny Range ENE of Kebeney volcano. Minor fissure-fed lava flows are located WNW. Early geological studies in the Sredinny Range (Ogorodov et al., 1972) assigned Holocene ages based on morphology, but later work noted that these volcanoes appear younger because they have less tephra cover than those in eastern Kamchatka.

properties.name: Leutongey
properties.summary: The Quaternary Leutongey basaltic shield-like volcano is at the south end of a NE-SW-trending graben about 20 km W of the crest of the central Sredinny Range.  A chain of cinder cones along the same trend cuts across the summit, and another larger cinder cone is on the S flank. The small basaltic Medveshiy stratovolcano is immediately to the SE.

properties.name: Tuzovsky
properties.summary: Three small overlapping Quaternary basaltic to basaltic andesite shield-like volcanoes are located NE of Leutongey volcano, west of the crest of the central Sredinny Range. Tuzovsky, the SW-most edifice, is the highest; Tvitunup is the northernmost, and Sredny is NE of Tuzovsky.

properties.name: Mezhdusopochny
properties.summary: Mezhdusopochny, a Quaternary basaltic shield-like volcano, lies at the NE end of a group of small shields in a NE-SW-trending graben extending west of the crest of the Sredinny Range north of Kebeny volcano. The volcano rises above the north shore of Lake Mezhdusopochny, and basaltic lava covers the graben floor to the south.

properties.name: Shishel
properties.summary: Shishel is a glacier-capped Quaternary basaltic shield-like volcano along the crest of the central Sredinny Range. It is on the east side of a broad graben containing a NE-SW-trending chain of overlapping small shields ranging from Leutongey on the SW to Mezhdusopochny on the NE. Small cinder cones are located S and SW of Shishel, and a major lava field is located on its NE flank.

properties.name: Alngey
properties.summary: Alngey, a small Quaternary stratovolcano, is immediately east of the large Pleistocene Tekletunup shield volcano, west of the crest of the northern Sredinny Range. It was constructed near the western margin of a large NE-SW-trending graben running along the axis of the Sredinny Range.

properties.name: Uka
properties.summary: Uka, a small Quaternary basaltic shield-like volcano, was constructed near the eastern margin of a large NE-SW-trending graben along the axis of the northern Sredinny Range. It is immediately east of the crest of the Sredinny Range, opposite Alngey volcano on the western side of the graben.

properties.name: Kaileney
properties.summary: Kaileney is a small Quaternary basaltic shield-like volcano near the eastern margin of a large NE-SW-trending graben running along the axis of the northern Sredinny Range. It is located NE of Uka, another shield volcano along the east side of the graben. A chain of E-W-trending cinder cones extends to the west from the summit.

properties.name: Plosky
properties.summary: Plosky, a small Quaternary basaltic shield-like volcano about 20 km W of the crest of the Sredinny Range, is the westernmost volcano of the northern Sredinny Range. It is located immediately north of the large Pleistocene Tekletunup volcano.

properties.name: Bely
properties.summary: The Quaternary basaltic Bely shield-like volcano in the northern Sredinny Range is topped by a small stratovolcano. The smaller Sergeeva and Keveneytunup shields are located to the south and east, respectively, and the late-Pleistocene Lagerny shield is to the SE. Keveneytunup is the highest of these volcanoes, slightly exceeding Bely.

properties.name: Snezhniy
properties.summary: Snezhniy is a small Quaternary basaltic shield-like volcano that was constructed near the eastern margin of a large NE-SW-trending graben running along the axis of the northern Sredinny Range. The smaller shield volcano Grechishkina is just NW, on the saddle between Snezhniy and Keveney volcanoes.

properties.name: Iktunup
properties.summary: The Quaternary basaltic to basaltic andesite shield-like Iktunup was constructed 5 km west of the lower, but larger shield of Tunipilyakum. The two volcanoes are located immediately NW and NE, respectively, of the Pleistocene Keveney volcano.

properties.name: Snegovoy
properties.summary: Glacier-covered Snegovoy is a late-Quaternary shield-like volcano topped by a small basaltic cone. It was constructed about 10 km ENE of Ostry volcano, near the NE end of the Sredinny Range. Early geological studies in the Sredinny Range (Ogorodov et al., 1972) assigned Holocene ages based on morphology, but later work noted that these volcanoes appear younger because they have less tephra cover than those in eastern Kamchatka.

properties.name: Iettunup
properties.summary: Iettunup and Lamutsky are small overlapping late-Quatenary basaltic to basaltic andesite shield-like volcanoes at the far NE end of the Sredinny Range. The summit of Iettunup is about 7 km NW of the summit cone of Lamutsky. Early geological studies in the Sredinny Range (Ogorodov et al., 1972) assigned Holocene ages based on morphology, but later work noted that these volcanoes appear younger because they have less tephra cover than those in eastern Kamcha…

properties.name: Voyampolsky
properties.summary: Voyampolsky and Kakhtana are two basaltic to basaltic andesite shield-like volcanoes that form the NW-most volcanoes of the Sredinny Range near the headwaters of the Kakhtana River. Early geological studies in the Sredinny Range (Ogorodov et al., 1972) assigned Holocene ages based on morphology, but later work noted that these volcanoes appear younger because they have less tephra cover than those in eastern Kamchatka.

properties.name: Vysokii
properties.summary: Vysokii and an unnamed volcano to the north are Pliocene stratovolcanoes with Pleistocene lava domes on or near their flanks (Masurenkov 1980).

properties.name: Tumanniy
properties.summary: Tumanniy is a Pliocene-Pleistocene shield-like volcano with flank lava domes (Masurenkov 1980).

properties.name: Ded i Baba
properties.summary: Ded i Baba (Ded and Baba) is an early Pleistocene shield-like volcano SW of Koshelev volcano; an unnamed mid-Pleistocene volcano with a small caldera breached to the east lies between these two volcanoes (Masurenkov 1980).

properties.name: Tretya Rechka
properties.summary: Tretya Rechka is an early Pleistocene shield-like volcano with a small caldera open to the SE (Masurenkov 1980).

properties.name: Kuzheten
properties.summary: Mid-Pleistocene shield-like volcano (Masurenkov 1980).

properties.name: Kuzanek
properties.summary: Pliocene to lower Pleistocene shield-like volcano (Masurenkov 1980).

properties.name: Igolki
properties.summary: Igolki and Bol'shiye Igolki are two lower to mid-Pleistocene shield-like volcanoes (Masurenkov 1980).

properties.name: Skalistiy
properties.summary: Pliocene to lower Pleistocene shield-like volcano (Masurenkov 1980).

properties.name: Perevalny
properties.summary: Perevalny is a small upper-Pleistocene shield volcano NNE of Khodutka volcano; an unnamed Pleistocene stratovolcano is located immediately NE of Perevalny (Masurenkov 1980).

properties.name: Krugliy
properties.summary: Upper Pleistocene shield volcano (Masurenkov 1980).

properties.name: Savan
properties.summary: Savan is a Pliocene to lower Pleistocene shield volcano (Masurenkov 1980).

properties.name: Malaya Ipelka
properties.summary: Malaya Ipelka is an isolated mid to late-Pleistocene volcanic massif rising above the SW coastal lowlands north of the Opala River (Masurenkov 1980).

properties.name: Kamen
properties.summary: Late-Pleistocene conical basaltic volcano (Masurenkov 1980).

properties.name: Ploskiy
properties.summary: The conical early Pleistocene basaltic Ploskiy volcano is located west of Asacha volcano and north of a large group of late Pleistocene to Holocene pyroclastic cones (Masurenkov, 1980).

properties.name: Vostochnaya Khodutka
properties.summary: Two lower to mid-Pleistocene shield-like volcanoes (Masurenkov 1980).

properties.name: Zheltiy
properties.summary: Small conical late Pleistocene basaltic volcano (Masurenkov, 1980).

properties.name: Tolmachev
properties.summary: Tolmacheva and Utes are conical basaltic volcanoes of late-Pleistocene age (Masurenkov 1980).

properties.name: Udochka
properties.summary: Udochka is a mid-Pleistocene shield-like volcano SW of Opala (Masurenkov 1980).

properties.name: Bolshaya Ipelka
properties.summary: Bolshaya Ipelka is a massive eroded lower Pleistocene shield-like volcano that covers a 32 x 42 km area west of the main volcanic zone of southern Kamchatka.  A Holocene cinder cone on the SE flank is listed separately in this compilation.

properties.name: Aak
properties.summary: Aak, Arik, and Pinachevsky are Pleistocene volcanoes along a ridge trending NW from Koryaksky volcano.  Abnormal shallow earthquakes occurred in August 1966 (Gorel'chik, 1969).

properties.name: Kupol
properties.summary: Kupol is a Pleistocene basaltic andesite stratovolcano (Luchitsky 1974).

properties.name: Kitkhoysky
properties.summary: Two Pleistocene shield-like volcanoes are located NW of Kupol and SW of Vershkinsky volcanoes (Erlich 1985, pers. comm.). Satellite imagery in Google Earth appears to show a 6-km-diameter caldera open to the N with a later cone or dome complex on the eastern side.

properties.name: Zhupanovskiye Vostriyaky
properties.summary: Large Pleistocene stratovolcano north of Zhupanova River

properties.name: Ditmara
properties.summary: Ditmara is a broad, low stratovolcano SE of Akademia Nauk caldera.

properties.name: Unana
properties.summary: Unana stratovolcano is of Pleistocene age; hot springs on the volcano are related to tectonic faults (Erlich 1985, pers. comm.).

properties.name: Adamozhets
properties.summary: Satellite imagery shows a 2-km cone with an open crater that appears to be a volcanic feature about 9 km SE of the original location provided by Erlich (1985, pers. comm.), who identified this as a Pleistocene volcano. It is about 35 km NW of the Uzon caldera.

properties.name: Bogachensky
properties.summary: Pleistocene shield-like volcano north of Kolkhozhny volcano (Erlich 1985, pers. comm.).

properties.name: Piip
properties.summary: Pleistocene shield-like volcano (Erlich 1985, pers. comm.).

properties.name: Konechnaya
properties.summary: Mid to upper Pleistocene shield-like volcano (Luchitsky 1974).

properties.name: Konradi
properties.summary: Vlasov (1967) notes postglacial activity of Konradi; later work indicates it is of Pleistocene age (Erlich 1985, pers. comm.).

properties.name: Tumrok
properties.summary: Mid to upper Pleistocene shield-like volcano (Luchitsky 1974).

properties.name: Iult
properties.summary: Iult (also spelled Iul't) is a large stratovolcano located north of Konradi volcano and NNW of the Gamchen volcanic complex. Lava domes on the lower northern and southern flanks were assigned a Holocene age by Luchitsky (1974), but Andreev et al. (1988) mapped them as late Pleistocene.

properties.name: Sokol
properties.summary: Mid to upper Pleistocene stratovolcano north of Konradi volcano (Luchitsky 1974).

properties.name: Zarechny
properties.summary: Zarechny is a low, forested volcano constructed in the lake-filled lowlands between Kliuchevskoi and Shiveluch volcanoes, and immediately S of Kharchinsky volcano. The 760-m-high edifice contains two nested calderas, both breached widely to the SE. The larger 4.5 x 3.7 km wide caldera is filled by an uneroded cone truncated by a 3.2 x 1.8 km wide caldera.

properties.name: Kharchinsky
properties.summary: Kharchinsky is a Pleistocene volcano immediately north of Zarechny volcano (Luchitsky, 1974) in the lowlands north of the Kamchatka River.  The magnesian basaltic volcano rises 1400 m above the surrounding plains.  It was constructed during the late Pleistocene and predates glacial moraines dated at 23,000-24,000 years ago.  Faulting and edifice failures have deeply affected the edifice, and debris-avalanche fans are found at its base.

properties.name: Eastern Kamchatka Arc at 56.5°N
properties.summary: A group of basaltic cinder cones is located north of Kharchinsky volcano in the lowlands SW of Sheveluch volcano. The cones and lava flows cover a broad area north of Kharchinsky and form a peninsula extending into Lake Kharchinsky.

properties.name: Lauchachan
properties.summary: Small late Pleistocene basaltic shield volcano SW of Ichinsky volcano (Ogorodov et al., 1972).

properties.name: Prodolny
properties.summary: Prodolny and Lauchan are adjacent Pleistocene shield volcanoes SW of Ichinsky volcano (Erlich 1985, pers. comm.).

properties.name: Kobalan
properties.summary: Pleistocene basaltic stratovolcano, SW of Ichinsky volcano (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Lyzyk
properties.summary: The small isolated Lyzyk volcano is probably of late-Pleistocene age (Erlich 1985, pers. comm.).

properties.name: Uchkoren
properties.summary: Uchkoren is a small Pleistocene volcano (Erlich 1985, pers. comm.).

properties.name: Tynua
properties.summary: Two Pleistocene Icelandic shield volcanoes (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Etopan
properties.summary: Late-Pleistocene Icelandic-type shield volcano (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Kimitina
properties.summary: Pleistocene basaltic stratovolcano (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Central Kamchatka Arc at 55.5°N
properties.summary: Pleistocene (Erlich 1985, pers. comm.).

properties.name: Ochchamo
properties.summary: Lower-Pleistocene shield volcano east of Ichinsky volcano (Erlich 1985, pers. comm.).

properties.name: Bolshoy Kozyrevsky
properties.summary: Lower-Pleistocene shield volcano (Erlich 1985, pers. comm.).

properties.name: Bolshaya Romanovka
properties.summary: Lower-Pleistocene shield volcano (Erlich 1985, pers. comm.).

properties.name: Central Kamchatka Arc at 55.9°N
properties.summary: Group of three Pleistocene stratovolcanoes (Erlich, 1985 pers. comm.).

properties.name: Bongabti
properties.summary: Early Pleistocene shield volcano (Ogorodov et al., 1972).

properties.name: Nosichan
properties.summary: Late-Pleistocene Icelandic shield volcano (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Buduli
properties.summary: Late Pleistocene shield volcano (Ogorodov et al., 1972).

properties.name: Kopkan
properties.summary: Late Pleistocene shield volcano; the Krugelenky shield to the NE along the regional NE-SW trend is listed with Kapkan (Erlich 1985, pers. comm.).

properties.name: Yanpat
properties.summary: Yanpat and Vetrovoy volcano to the north are late-Pleistocene Icelandic-type shield volcanoes (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Chavycha
properties.summary: Chavycha and Olka volcano to the north are mid to late-Pleistocene Icelandic-type shield volcanoes (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Malaya Ketepana
properties.summary: Malaya Ketepana is one of several large shield volcanoes along the western margin of the Sredinny Range.  Smaller Icelandic-type shield volcanoes are located on the south flank and NE of Malaya Ketepana.

properties.name: Bolshoy Ketepana
properties.summary: Bolshoy Ketepana is a large isolated early Pleistocene shield volcano on the west side of the Sredinny Range (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Central Kamchatka Arc at 57.0°N
properties.summary: Pleistocene shield volcano (Erlich, 1985 pers. comm.).

properties.name: Ovalny
properties.summary: Mid to late-Pleistocene shield volcano (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Tigilsky
properties.summary: The lower to mid-Pleistocene Tigilsky shield volcano (Ogorodov et al. 1972) appears to have a 2-km-wide crater just SE of the summit. An area on the W flank was previously listed as an Unnamed Holocene basaltic shield volcano. The morphology as observed in satellite imagery suggests that the "shield" is simply an erosional feature along a volcanic ridge of the larger edifice.

properties.name: Perevalovyi
properties.summary: Mid-Pleistocene shield volcano with a summit caldera (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Maly Alney
properties.summary: The mid to late-Pleistocene basaltic stratovolcanoes of Maly Alney and Polovinny are located SE of Alney volcano (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Maly Chekchebonay
properties.summary: Mid-Pleistocene shield volcano with Hawaiian-type summit caldera (Ogorodov et al. 1972; Erlich 1986).

properties.name: Bolshoy Chekchebonay
properties.summary: Lower-Pleistocene shield volcano with Hawaiian-type summit caldera (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Kireunsky
properties.summary: Late-Pleistocene Icelandic-type shield volcano (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Dvukhyurtochny
properties.summary: Late-Pleistocene Icelandic-type shield volcano (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Central Kamchatka Arc at 56.9°N
properties.summary: Group of mid-Pleistocene extrusive lava domes (Erlich, 1985 pers. comm.).

properties.name: Kalgauch
properties.summary: Late-Pleistocene basaltic stratovolcano (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Kunkhilok
properties.summary: Late-Pleistocene basaltic stratovolcano east of the Sredinny Range crest (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Shlen
properties.summary: Shlen is a large mid-Pleistocene shield volcano west of the main Sredinny Range (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Pirozhnikova
properties.summary: Late-Pleistocene basaltic stratovolcano (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Kamenisty
properties.summary: Late-Pleistocene basaltic stratovolcano (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Tekletunup
properties.summary: Tekletunup is a large eroded Pliocene to lower-Pleistocene shield volcano (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Ulvaney
properties.summary: Late Pleistocene shield volcano (Ogorodov et al., 1972).

properties.name: Mutny
properties.summary: Late Pleistocene shield volcano (Ogorodov et al., 1972).

properties.name: Khuvkhoitun
properties.summary: The late-Pleistocene complex stratovolcano Khuvkhoitun forms the highest peak of the northern Sredinny Range.  Two small late-Pleistocene shield volcanoes are located immediately to the NE (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Keveney
properties.summary: Keveney is a late-Pleistocene Icelandic-type shield volcano (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Langtutkin
properties.summary: Langtutkin is a late-Pleistocene Icelandic-type shield volcano east of the crest of the Sredinny Range (Ogorodov et al. 1972).

properties.name: Anjuisky
properties.summary: The Anjuisky (Anyuy) volcano group consists of fissure vents and small pyroclastic cones, the largest of which is 120-m high and is capped by a 300-m-wide crater. The initial fissure eruptions produced trachybasaltic lava flows 15-17 km long that covered an area of 100 km2.

properties.name: Balagan-Tas
properties.summary: Balagan-Tas is a cinder cone constructed along a fault on the SW flank of the Momskiy Mountains in the NE part of Russia's Sakha Republic. A poorly preserved crater fed subalkaline basaltic lava flows that covered an area of 4-5 km2. A Potassium-Argon date of 300,000 years was obtained (Prokopiev, 2007 pers. comm.).

properties.name: Vitim Volcanic Field
properties.summary: Volcanism in the Vitim Volcanic Field dates back to the Miocene and covers an area of about 4,500 km2 east of the northern part of Lake Baikal. The most voluminous activity took place from the Miocene to Pleistocene. Most of the volcanic centers are located in the NW part of the field (Johnson et al., 2005). Mantle xenoliths are found in several locations. Ivanov et al. (2015) mapped it as Pleistocene and reported ages between 0.5 and 1.2 Ma.

properties.name: Tunkin Depression
properties.summary: The Tunkin Depression volcanic field (also known as the Tunka Depression) covers a broad area immediately west of the SW tip of Lake Baikal. The Khobok group of basaltic cinder cones near the village of Tunka, one of five groups of cinder cones characterized by some sources as late-Pleistocene to Holocene in age, has the largest concentration of vents.

properties.name: East Tuva Volcanic Field
properties.summary: The large East Tuva volcanic field is located WNW of the SW tip of Lake Baikal and N of the Mongolian border. The gently sloping Azas Plateau, also known as the East Tuva Plateau, the Northeast Tuva Plateau, or the Khamsara-Biykhem Plateau, covers an area of about 2,000 km2. Its glacially dissected surface is cut by broad valleys and contains several table-like mountains composed of hyaloclastites and lava flows, and has numerous small scoria cones.

properties.name: Dgida Basin
properties.summary: The Dgida Basin volcanic field, also known as the Dzhida Basin, is located south of the SW tip of Lake Baikal, near the border with Mongolia. One of a series of approximately E-W-trending depressions, the basin contains Quaternary lava flows and cinder cones ranging from 55 to 240 m in height. At least two stages of volcanism are present, the first of which includes lava flows overlying the 20 m terrace of the Dgida, Darkhintuy, and Khammey rivers.

properties.name: Khanuy Gol Volcanic Field
properties.summary: The Khanuy Gol (also spelled Hanui or Hanuy Gol) Volcanic Field is also known as the Chanuj Gol or Bulgan volcanic field. It consists of a group of 10 olivine-basaltic lava and cinder cones in west-central Mongolia about 150 km WNW of the capital city of Ulaanbaatar. The field covers a 3,500 km2 plain along the Khanuy River and in drainages to the east.

properties.name: Dariganga Volcanic Field
properties.summary: The Dariganga volcanic field, located in SE Mongolia near the China border, consists of more than 200 lava and cinder cones erupted from NE-trending parallel fissures. The cones range in height from 25 to 300 m, and vary from partially eroded to completely preserved. Compositionally they are more Na-rich than the K-rich rocks of northern and central Mongolia, and consist of basaltic, trachybasaltic, and foiditic rocks.

properties.name: Henglianghu-Dongyuehu Volcanic Field
properties.summary: A volcanic zone spanning ~350 km E-W in NE Tibet was identified by Tong et al. (1988) as having multiple Cenozoic volcanoes. Five locations were named on the small-scale map (Yongbocuo, Bamaoqiongzhong, Kushuihuan-Beishan, Heiguotou, and Yuyiehu). Although only Bamaoqiongzhong is mentioned in later research, this may be due to unknown synonyms or other language translations.

properties.name: Heishibeihu
properties.summary: Listed as an unnamed Quaternary volcano by IAVCEI (1973), it was included in a summary list of northern Tibetan volcanic locations by Guo et al. (2006) under the name Heishibeihu with a cited 14C date of 670,000 years. A small shield feature is present, with a large lava field. Located ~115 km ESE of the Ashikule Volcanic Field, SE of the Altyn Tagh fault in the Songpan-Ganzi Terrane, the lava field covers 355 km2 (Guo et al., 2006).

properties.name: Ulagh Muztagh
properties.summary: An unnamed basaltic volcano was listed in this general area by IAVCEI (1973). Although mislocated ~100 km E (1° of longitude), this entry may have been referencing the small mountain ridge of Ulagh Muztagh, ~30 km long and largely snow-covered. It was mapped as 11-4.0 Ma rhyolites in Wang et al. (2016, see citations).

properties.name: Longhai
properties.summary: Longhai is a late-Cenozoic volcano (Tong et al. 1988) at the south end of the Zhemin Volcano Group of Chen (1986).

properties.name: Jianghui Group
properties.summary: The Jianghui Volcano Group consists of remnants of about 20 basaltic hills.  Comparatively well-preserved craters exist along the eastern shore of Nushanhu and the western shore of Chaohu. The basalt is of early Quaternary age (Chen 1986; Whitford-Stark 1987, pers. comm.).

properties.name: Nushan
properties.summary: Truncated cone of Pliocene-lower Pleistocene age (IAVCEI).

properties.name: Yichuan
properties.summary: Late-Cenozoic volcano (Tong et al. 1988).

properties.name: Tangy'n
properties.summary: Late-Cenozoic volcano; name appears as "Tangy n" in Tong et al. (1988).

properties.name: Huixian
properties.summary: Late-Cenozoic volcano (Tong et al. 1988).

properties.name: Heibei Plain
properties.summary: Late-Cenozoic volcano (Tong et al. 1988).

properties.name: Datong-Fengzen
properties.summary: The Datong-Fengzhen volcano group, also known as Ta-T'ung or Fanjiatun, is located at the intersection of two regional fault zones.  The volcanic field contains about 80 volcanic vents, including cinder cones and small lava domes.  The central Datong group contains 12 cones.  An historical eruption reported during the 5th century (Chen 1986) has been shown to have originated from spontaneous combustion of a Jurassic coal seam (Zhang 1989, pers. comm.).

properties.name: Chifeng
properties.summary: Late-Cenozoic volcano (Tong et al. 1988).

properties.name: Dalainuoer
properties.summary: Tapponnier and Molnar (1977) documented from satellite images a large volcanic field with fresh features suggesting possible Holocene eruptions. Hang (1989, pers. comm.) indicates that extensive dating by Yang indicates the youngest eruptions were of late Pleistocene age.

properties.name: Nuomin
properties.summary: The Nuomin volcanic field, identified as Shatu in Ogara (1969) and Whiford-Stark (1987), is dominated by monogenetic cones and lava flows that cover about 600 km2 (Zhao and others, 2014). K-Ar dating by Fan and others (2012, cited in Zhao and others, 2014) indicated eruptions between 2.3 and 0.13 Ma. The most recent activity was at the Sifang Mountain, which is the southernmost cone of the group and contains a small lake in the summit crater.

properties.name: Jianshan
properties.summary: Jianshan volcano (at the Jianshan Farm) is located NW of the Wudalianchi volcanic field. Zhao and others (2014) reported that this isolated monogenetic cinder cone was K–Ar dated at 0.12 ± 0.02 Ma.

properties.name: Erkeshan
properties.summary: Two adjacent volcanic cones are located just NE of the city of Kedong in the Heilongjiang Province of far northeastern of China. The larger eastern cone is about 700 m in diameter, and the smaller western one is 600 m. A third circular feature about 200 m in diameter forms a very low (12 m high) hill about 1 km NW of the western cone.

properties.name: Dunhua
properties.summary: Dunhua was described by Whitford-Stark (1987) as being composed of flows of two or three different ages.

properties.name: Ch'uga-ryong
properties.summary: An area of extensive basaltic lava flows occupies a graben, the NNE-SSW-trending Ch'uga-ryong rift, that cuts diagonally across the border between North and South Korea. As summarized by Whitford-Stark (1987), Tomita (1969) noted that a 40-km-long lava flow originated from the low Ap-san shield volcano, which has a 200-m-wide summit crater and more than 20 satellitic cones, and another voluminous late-Pleistocene lava flow is 60 km long.

properties.name: Koksan-Singye
properties.summary: Lava flows located between the cities of Koksan and Singye were listed as probably active in last 2,000 years by IAVCEI (1973). However, Whitford-Stark (1987) lists it as Pleistocene and Tomita (1967) states there has been no Holocene volcanism on the Korean Peninsula.

properties.name: Sergief
properties.summary: Sergief is a small stratovolcano on SW Atka Island whose age is poorly known. The SW part of the island is older and less topographically rugged than the NE part of the island. It was tentatively listed as a young volcano in the Post-Miocene Volcanoes of the World catalog of the International Association of Volcanology and Chemistry of the Earth's Interior (1973), but the age of its latest eruption is not precisely known.

properties.name: Isanotski Peaks
properties.summary: Rugged pinnacles form the summit of the deeply eroded Isanotski Peaks stratovolcano, locally known as Ragged Jack, at the center of a group of three volcanoes on eastern Unimak Island. Four poorly documented eruptions were noted in the 18th and 19th centuries. However, Miller et al.

properties.name: Adagdak
properties.summary: Mount Adagdak, at the NE tip of Adak Island, lies across Andrew Lagoon from Mount Moffett volcano and ~15 km NNE of the town of Adak. It consists of a small stratovolcano capping an older shield volcano exposed on the southern side of the complex. An andesitic lava dome fills the summit crater. A late-stage basaltic lava dome was constructed on the SE flank, and a phreatic vent is located on the W flank of the shield volcano.

properties.name: Gilbert
properties.summary: Mount Gilbert is deeply eroded and an area of former solfataric activity appears to have been glaciated. Solfataric activity had ceased between 1942 and 1945 (Byers and Barth 1953).

properties.name: Trader Mountain
properties.summary: Trader Mountain is a small dacitic stratocone-like feature with an extrusive dome; lava flows dip away from the center in all directions (Chris Nye, oral commun., 2007).  Wilson and others (1995) alternatively described Trader Mountain as a hypabyssal dacite plug, and report a potassium-argon age of 0.98+/- 0.05 Ma (F.H. Wilson and Nora Shew, unpub. data, 1988).

properties.name: Blue Mountain
properties.summary: The Blue Mountain lava dome cluster immediately west of Upper Ugashik Lake consists of 13 dacitic lava domes. An Ar-Ar date of about 632,000 years was obtained from the highest dome.

properties.name: Gertrude Creek
properties.summary: An ice-scoured basaltic scoria cone and associated lava-flow apron lies at Getrude Creek about 5 km NE of Becharof Lake.  The cone was constructed near the trace of the Bruin Bay fault and was Argon-Argon dated at about 500,000 years BP (Hildreth et al., 2003).

properties.name: Devils Desk
properties.summary: Devils Desk, which rises 450 m above the top of Hook Glacier to its west, is the eroded neck of a former stratovolcano, most of which has been removed by extensive erosion.  Three radial dikes exposed as ridges extend from the volcano toward the east.  Devils Desk lies at the NE end of a glacier-mantled range containing small closely spaced volcanic centers that extends from Snowy Mountain, NE of Mount Katmai.

properties.name: Savonovski River Cluster
properties.summary: A group of small Pleistocene stratovolcanoes and a scoria cone lies behind the volcanic front near the headwaters of the Savonovski River, NW of the Denison to Devils Creek alignment of volcanoes. Dated ages range from about 88,000 to 390,000 years (Hildreth et al., 2003).

properties.name: Double Glacier
properties.summary: Double Glacier volcano is a Pleistocene lava dome complex forming a nunatak in Double Glacier.  Potassium-Argon dates range from 627 to 887 thousand years ago (Reed et al. 1992).  Nearby Double Peak, 5 km to the north, was once thought to be a volcano (Coats 1950, IAVCEI 1973), but reconnaissance mapping indicates the peak probably consists of Jurassic plutonic rocks (Reed et al. 1992).

properties.name: Nunivak Island
properties.summary: Nunivak Island contains about 60 cinder cones and four maars; the surface of the island is dominated by thin pahoehoe lava flows that form a carapace over Cretaceous sedimentary rocks. The 110-km-wide permafrost-covered island lies about 30 km off the coast of SW Alaska.
