properties.summary: Early investigators considered Sverre to be of postglacial age based on its location in a glacially carved valley.  Semevskii (1965) assigned an age between 6,500 and 4,000 years before present (BP) marine terraces. A more detailed study of glacial and volcanic stratigraphy suggests an age between 100,000 and 250,000 BP (Skjelkvale et al., 1989).

properties.name: Corvo
properties.summary: The 4 x 6 km island of Corvo is located at the NW end of the Azores archipelago, west of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. A 2-km-wide caldera on the NW side of the island is the most prominent feature. The caldera floor contains several small cinder cones and two shallow lakes.

properties.name: Sao Vicente
properties.summary: The 15 x 25 km island of Sao Vicente contains mafic lavas covering prominent peninsulas on the eastern and NE sides (Mitchell-Thome, 1976). The largest indentation on this island with an irregular shoreline is formed by a caldera on the NW coast that is breached by the sea and forms the setting for the port of Mindelo, the island's largest village.

properties.name: Santo Antao
properties.summary: The 20 x 40 km dominantly volcanic island of Santo Antao is the NW-most of the Cape Verde Islands. Volcanic activity dates back to the Pliocene and continued into the late Pleistocene. A large 7-km-wide E-facing depression, Cha de Morte, was thought at one point to be a caldera, but was later interpreted as an erosional feature. Much of the island is covered by phonolitic pumice deposits of the Cao Grande Pumice, erupted about 200,000 years ago.

properties.name: Sao Nicolau
properties.summary: Sao Nicolau, located the eastern end of an E-W-trending chain of islands in the NW Cape Verde islands, was constructed in four stages dating back to the Pliocene. The last two stages took place during the Pleistocene, and the youngest stage produced scoria cones and lava flows about 50,000 years ago.

properties.name: Trindade
properties.summary: The small island of Trindade lies more than halfway between Brazil and the Mid-Atlantic Ridge at the eastern end of the Vitória-Trindade Ridge, an E-W-trending chain of submarine volcanoes and guyots extending about 1,100 km from the continental shelf off the Brazilian coast.  It is a dissected volcanic island with numerous phonolitic lava domes and steep-sided volcanic plugs.

properties.name: Martin Vaz
properties.summary: The Martin Vaz archipelago lies 48 km east of Trindade Island, about 1750 km west of the Mid-Atantic Ridge. A larger islet, Martin Vaz, is adjacent to three smaller ones. K-Ar ages of about 1.5 Ma and less than 0.73 Ma were obtained.

properties.name: Gough Island
properties.summary: Gough Island, also known as Diego Alvarez, lies about 340 km SE of the Tristan da Cunha island group.  The shield volcano was active from about 2.5 to 0.13 million years ago.

properties.name: Inaccessible Island
properties.summary: Inaccessible Island, located about 40 km SW of Tristan da Cunha, was Potassium-Argon age dated at 6 +/- 1.5 million years ago (Baker et al., 1964), but more recent dates of about 1 million have been obtained (Cliff et al., 1991). The island is the remnant of a stratovolcano centered about 2 km SW.

properties.name: Northern Victoria Land
properties.summary: A large number of isolated basaltic scoria cones are located throughout Antarctica's northern Victoria Land near the western coast of the Ross Sea, not clearly associated with the larger stratovolcanoes. One lava flow on the southern side of Cosmonaut Glacier, SW of Mount Overlord, spilled onto the glacier and diverted it, but has not yet been removed by erosion or covered by ice.

properties.name: Waesche
properties.summary: Mount Waesche is the southernmost of a N-S chain of volcanoes in central Marie Byrd Land, 20 km SW of Pliocene Mount Sidley. The Waesche shield was constructed around 1.0 Ma on the SE rim of the 10-km-wide Chang Peak caldera; pre-caldera Chang Peak lavas were erupted about 1.6 Ma. Satellitic cinder cones, some aligned along radial fissures, are located on the SW flank.

properties.name: Siple
properties.summary: Mount Siple is a shield volcano that forms an island along the Pacific Ocean coast of Antarctica's Marie Byrd Land. The massive 1,800 km3 volcano is truncated by a 4-5 km summit caldera and is ringed by tuff cones at sea level. A possible eruption cloud observed on satellite images on 18 September and 4 October 1988 was considered to result from atmospheric effects, after low-level aerial observations revealed no evidence of recent eruptions.

properties.name: Toney Mountain
properties.summary: Toney Mountain in east-central Marie Byrd Land is a 50-km-long volcanic massif with a 3-km-wide summit caldera and several satellitic cinder cones. Several small cinder cones occur along the crest of the massif, which is almost entirely covered by glaciers. A felsic sample from the summit area gave a Potassium-Argon date of 500,000 years.

properties.name: Peter I Island
properties.summary: The 11 x 19 km Peter I Island in the Bellingshausen Sea opposite Ellsworth Land is a shield-like volcano with a 100-m-wide circular crater at its summit.The island was discovered by the Russian explorer Bellingshausen in 1821; extensive summer pack ice and its isolated location far from regular shipping lanes have restricted visits. Dated samples range from 350,000 to 100,000 years old (Prestvik et al. 1990).

properties.name: Seal Nunataks Volcanic Field
properties.summary: The Seal Nunataks are a group of 16 isolated nunataks emerging from the Larsen Ice Shelf east of Graham Land Peninsula. Most of the larger nunataks are considered to represent separate volcanic vents erupted in a shallow-water environment.

properties.name: Gaussberg
properties.summary: Gaussgberg is an ice-free conical mountain composed primarily of subglacial eruptive products.  No vent has been located and its present morphology is thought to result from glacial and subaerial erosion of a once-larger mountain that was formed about 55,000 years ago (LeMasurier and Thomson 1990).

properties.name: Adare Peninsula
properties.summary: The Adare Peninsula is a complex of overlapping shield volcanoes forming the northernmost volcanic pile of the Hallet Volcanic Province.  Hamilton (1972) considered uneroded cinder cones at Cape McCormick to be of Holocene age, but similar-looking Antarctic cones have proved to be as old as Tertiary.

properties.name: Rittmann, Mount
properties.summary: Mount Rittmann, a roughly 8 x 5 km caldera under the Aviator Glacier in the Melbourne Volcanic Province, has been dated at between about 4 and 0.07 million years ago (Martin et al., 2010). Active fumaroles, heated ground, and ice and snow hummocks occur near the caldera rim.

properties.name: Franklin Island
properties.summary: Franklin Island is a 2 x 7.6 km remnant of a shield volcano whose vent was located to the east. IAVCEI (1973) assigns a Quaternary age. The only radiometric date available is a Potassium-Argon date of 4.8 +/- 2.0 Ma (LeMasurier and Thomson 1990). Bathymetric mapping in 2004 identified the Franklin Volcanic Field, a regional high with clusters of submarine cones extending 80 km long and up to 40 km wide (Smith, 2004).

properties.name: Beaufort Island
properties.summary: Beaufort Island is an eroded remnant of a Quaternary volcano (Calkin and Nichol 1972). LeMasurier and Thomson (1990) indicate its age is unknown.

properties.name: Terror
properties.summary: Mount Terror is a large basaltic shield volcano forming the eastern portion of Ross Island with numerous pyroclastic cones and lava domes. The youngest dated rocks are 0.82 million years ago (Ma) from the lower slopes of Terror and 0.8 Ma from the summit of Terra Nova, a large basaltic cone on the W flank (LeMasurier and Thomson, 1990).

properties.name: Taylor Valley
properties.summary: Taylor Valley contains numerous basaltic cinder cones, the youngest of which is Potassium-Argon dated 1.57 million years ago. Similar Pliocene volcanism took place in the Wright Valley to the north (LeMasurier and Thomson 1990).

properties.name: Bursey
properties.summary: Two coalescing shield volcanoes with 4-5 km diameter summit calderas, Hutt Peak on the east and Koerner Bluff on the west, form Mount Bursey. Potassium-Argon dates indicate both volcanoes were constructed during the Miocene; the youngest dated rock is 490,000 years old, from a cone on the Hutt Peak caldera rim (LeMasurier and Thomson, 1990).

properties.name: Obiglio
properties.summary: Mt. Obiglio is a strombolian-phreatomagmatic cone on Grant Island with a Potassium-Argon date of 0.51 million years ago (LeMasurier and Thomson, 1990).

properties.name: Shepard Island
properties.summary: Shepard Island consists of a group of tuff cones and a possible lava dome.  The youngest dated rock at Worley Point has a Potassium-Argon date of 0.42 million years ago (LeMasurier and Thomson 1990).

properties.name: Crary Group
properties.summary: The Crary Mountains consist of two large shield volcanoes, Mount Frakes and Mount Steere, and the smaller Mount Rees and Boyd Ridge volcanoes. Mount Steere is dissected, but the younger Mount Frakes is relatively undissected has had flank vent activity as late as 1.7 million K-Ar years ago (LeMasurier and Thomson, 1990).

properties.name: Murphy
properties.summary: Mount Murphy is a glacially dissected basaltic-trachytic shield volcano that formed during the Miocene. A Potassium-Argon date on a cone of 900,000 years indicates that flank activity resumed much later during the Pleistocene (LeMasurier, 1972; LeMasurier et al., 1990).

properties.name: Beethoven Peninsula
properties.summary: The Beethoven Peninsula contains nine nunataks consisting of basaltic lava flows and associated hyaloclastites.  No primary volcanic edifice is preserved and it is not clear whether the exposures represent individual volcanic vents or a volcanic field.  The youngest dated rocks are less than one million years old (LeMasurier and Thomson 1990).

properties.name: Brabant Island
properties.summary: Isolated exposures of the Bahia Bouquet Formation occur on Brabant Island; a Potassium-Argon date of less than 1 million years was obtained from a rock at the northern end of the island. The region has been poorly studied (LeMasurier and Thomson, 1990).

properties.name: Hut Point Peninsula
properties.summary: Hut Point Peninsula consists of a 20-km-long line of basaltic scoria cones south of Erebus. Potassium-Argon dates range from 1.34 to 0.44 million years ago (LeMasurier and Thomson, 1990). Martin et al. (2010) listed a 0.5 Ma date.

properties.name: White Island
properties.summary: White Island is a mostly ice-covered volcanic complex at the northern end of the island consisting of two shield volcanoes and overlying pyroclastic cones. The youngest Potassium-Argon date obtained was 0.17 million years ago and there is no evidence of Holocene activity.

properties.name: Black Island
properties.summary: A series of basaltic pyroclastic cones and trachytic lava domes form Black Island, in the Ross Sea west of White Island. Potassium-Argon dates of 3.4 Ma were obtained (LeMasurier and Thomson 1990).  Martin et al. (2010) reported dates of 3.8-1.69 million years.

properties.name: Transantarctic Mountain Foothills
properties.summary: Volcanic rocks in the Transantarctic Mountain Foothills have been radiometrically dated at between 14 and 0.9 million years (Martin et al., 2010).

properties.name: Mason Spur
properties.summary: An older trachytic volcanic complex at Mason Spur is overlain by a younger sequence consisting of a trachytic dome, tuff rings, and numerous basanite and tephrite cinder cones. Several lava flows drape over the bluffs, and may be less than 100,000 years old (LeMasurier and Thomson, 1990).

properties.name: Livingston-Greenwich Islands
properties.summary: Several small eroded tuff cones remnants and volcanic plugs are located on northern Livingston and Greenwich Island. Dated samples from two location are younger than 500,000 years ago (LeMasurier and Thomson, 1990).

properties.name: Tabarin Peninsula
properties.summary: Extensive plateau basalts on the southern Tabarin Peninsula may have erupted from fissures, small centers, or a large shield volcano. Basalts and tuff breccias are also found on Jonassen, Andersson, Rosamel and Dundee Islands. The only radiometric ages are 1.1 and 0.9 million years ago from rocks on the Tabarin Peninsula (LeMasurier and Thomson, 1990).

properties.name: Argo Point
properties.summary: Argo Point is a small scoria cone on the Jason Peninsula for which Potassium-Argon dates of 1.4 and 0.9 million years ago have been obtained (LeMasurier and Thomson, 1990).

properties.name: Lenderut
properties.summary: Mapped as Pleistocene (Guth and Wood, 2014).

properties.name: Shombole
properties.summary: Mapped as Pleistocene (Guth and Wood, 2014).

properties.name: Discovery
properties.summary: Mount Discovery is a central volcano that Potassium-Argon dating indicates formed about 5.3 million years ago. The youngest flank cones have been dated at about 1.87 million years ago (LeMasurier and Thomson, 1990).

properties.name: Bowie Seamount
properties.summary: Final volcanism post-dates the 18,000 years before present upper marine terrace, and is thought to have continued into postglacial time (Herzer, 1971).

properties.name: Tuzo Wilson Knolls
properties.summary: Volcanic rocks from the Tuzo Wilson Knolls were most likely erupted since a drop in the sedimentation rate following sea level rise at end of the last glaciation. They are considered to be the current location of a hotspot that formed the Kodiak-Bowie seamount chain (Chase, 1977). A Potassium-Argon date of 55,000 +/- 55,000 years before present was obtained by Cousens et al. (1985).

properties.name: Dzau
properties.summary: The Dzau (Java) volcanic center produced fissure eruptions of andesitic lavas between 200 and 100 ka (Chernyshev et al, 2002).

properties.name: Vance Segment
properties.summary: The entire Juan de Fuca Ridge is an active spreading center, though there have been no eruptions observed or dates along the Vance Segment. This segment lies between Cleft Segment (the southern-most of the JdfR) to the south, and Axial Seamount to the north.

properties.name: Central Segment
properties.summary: Central Gorda Ridge between the Jackson Segment to the N and the Phoenix Segment to the S.

properties.name: Phoenix Segment
properties.summary: Southern Gorda Ridge segment just N of the Escanaba Segment.

properties.name: Simacak, Uruk
properties.summary: Converted from subfeature of Singkut caldera. Mapped as part of the Pliocene-Pleistocene QTvk unit (see Harahap, 2011; Aldiss et al., 1983; Cameron et al., 1982).

properties.name: Barus
properties.summary: Converted from subfeature of Singkut caldera. Mapped as part of the late Pleistocene Qvbr unit of andesitic lavas and pyroclastics (see Harahap, 2011; Aldiss et al., 1983; Cameron et al., 1982).

properties.name: Dorobu
properties.summary: The Dorobu caldera, 13 x 6 km in diameter, is located within the southern part of NE Honshu about 10 km W of Takaharayama volcano. Miura and Tamai (1998) note that many other volcanoes formed during the late Miocene-Pliocene are within a 40 x 40 km area known as the Minami-Aizu geothermal field, including Okukinu, Kawaji, Yunishigawa, Tokusa, Yaso, Sannotoge, and Furumachi.

properties.name: Kasuga 3
properties.summary: Kasuga 3 is the southern-most of three volcanoes forming the Kasuga seamount chain, which trends SSW from the volcanic front of the Izu-Marianas arc. Embley et al. (2004) found no evidence of continuing hydrothermal activity.

properties.name: Eifuku
properties.summary: Seamount N of Daikoku in the northern Marianas Arc.

properties.name: East Neh
properties.summary: Walker et al. (2009) dated basalts along the East Neh fault at 1.45-1.75, 1.69-1.79, and 4.71-4.91 Ma. Volcanic deposits are strung out along perhaps 50 km on either side of the fault.

properties.name: San Diego
properties.summary: Although the San Diego maar has been known and described by Servicio Geologico Colombiana, along with dating by Toro (1988) that placed the most recent activity in the late Pleistocene-early Holocene, work by Borrero et al. (2016) provides a more comprehensive understanding of this volcano. The NNE-elongated crater is about 1.5 x 2.1 km and contains a lake about 230 m below the crater rim.

properties.name: Escondido, El
properties.summary: Identified by the Servicio Geologico Colombiano in a press release in February 2015, this area of a partially collapsed crater and lava domes is covered in thick vegetation. SGC scientists tentatively estimated that the last eruption was 30 ka, but noted that there are hot springs in the area.

properties.name: Etrusk
properties.summary: As described by Oyan et al. (2010), the Pliocene Etrüsk volcano is one of the major volcanic centers of eastern Anatolia, just NE of Lake Van. There is a ~5-km-wide open caldera near the center of the volcano, with the Pleistocene Karniyak scoria cone about 11 km away on the SW flank near the lake. K-Ar age determinations by Oyan et al. (2010) indicate that the main volcanic edifice was formed between 4.3 and 3.9 Ma, ending with caldera collapse.

properties.name: Pacific-Antarctic Ridge at 50.5°S
properties.summary: A basalt dredge sample Ar-Ar dated by Koppers et al. (2004) was 1.110 +/- 0.055 Ma. This seamount is about 90 km NW of Lonsdale Seamount and 400 km N of the Hollister Ridge 1991 acoustic signal location. It is near the extreme eastern end of the Louisville Seamount Chain where it intersects the Pacific-Antarctic Ridge, near where some models locate the Louisville hotspot (Vlastelic and Dosso, 2005).

properties.name: Putoto
properties.summary: Seamount in the northern Kermadec arc, about 160 km N of Raoul Island.

properties.name: Hingatungan
properties.summary: Undated Quaternary volcano mapped as Quaternary immediately N of Silago (Sajona et al., 1997).

properties.name: Lobi
properties.summary: Mapped as Quaternary by Sajona et al. (1997). Listed as inactive by PHIVOLCS.

properties.name: Pacdahauan
properties.summary: Volcanic features mapped as Quaternary by Sajona et al. (1997) on the Leyte Island peninsula south of Biliran Island.

properties.name: Undurer
properties.summary: Lahitte et al. (2003b) noted that "Despite poor constraints on timing of emplacement, Undurer and Babb-Olou volcanoes seem to have been more or less contemporaneous, erupting about 2 Myr ago...."

properties.name: Babba'Olou
properties.summary: Lahitte et al. (2003b) noted that "Despite poor constraints on timing of emplacement, Undurer and Babba'Olou volcanoes seem to have been more or less contemporaneous, erupting about 2 Myr ago...."

properties.name: Baqarah, Jabal
properties.summary: This isolated cone surrounded by lava flows about 18 km NE of the southern part of the Harrat al Birk field was considered to be similar in age to Jibal Haylah (54 km N), dated as Pleistocene by Coleman et al. (1983).

properties.name: Gaeta Bay Volcanic Field
properties.summary: The Gaeta Bay Volcanic Field consists of a group of eight buried submarine volcanoes of early to mid-Pleistocene age (Torrente and Milia, 2013). This volcanism is generally characterized by thick lava flows and volcaniclastic deposits. The entire volcanic field is up to 1,500 m thick.

properties.name: Skookum Creek
properties.summary: The Alaska Volcano Observatory describes this volcano as follows, from Miller and Richter (1994): "The Skookum Creek eruptive center is an erosionally dissected complex that may, in part, be as young as Quaternary. It consists principally of a series of rhyolite, rhyodacite, and andesite domes and their associated pyroclastic deposits, with an age of about 3.7 Ma, and an extensive sequence of relatively flat-lying andesite flows, some of which have been da…

properties.name: Jos Plateau
properties.summary: Volcanic features on the Jos Plateau include domes, single vents, and clusters of 3-4 cones aligned mainly NW-SE (Lar et al., 2013). Preliminary K-Ar dating of volcanic features reported by Lar et al. (2013) showed an age range of 2.5-1.34 Ma.

properties.name: Kumba Volcanic Field
properties.summary: Volcanic field SW of Tombel Graben and NNE of Mount Cameroon (within rectangular area of 4°48'15"N, 9°30'E and 4°24'15"N, 9°5'E). This area is known for the maar lakes Barombe Mbo, Barombi Koto, and Mboandong.

properties.name: Baldface Mountain
properties.summary: The Baldface Mountain Volcanic Field is part of the Anahim Volcanic Belt in central British Columbia, between the Itcha Range and Nazko Cone. The youngest Ar-Ar age found by Kuehn et al. (2015) was 0.91 Ma from a hawaiite flow 6 km SE of Baldface Mountain.

properties.name: Nichiyo Seamount
properties.summary: Nichiyo, one of the Shichiyo Seamounts, named for the seven days of the week ("Sunday"), lies south of Sofugan volcano. No hydrothermal activity or other unrest has been noted here, but it is assumed to be at least Pleistocene.

properties.name: Getsuyo Seamount
properties.summary: Getsuyo, one of the Shichiyo Seamounts, named for the seven days of the week ("Monday"), lies south of Sofugan volcano. No hydrothermal activity or other unrest has been noted here, but it is assumed to be at least Pleistocene.

properties.name: Kayo Seamount
properties.summary: Kayo, one of the Shichiyo Seamounts, named for the seven days of the week ("Tuesday"), lies south of Sofugan volcano. No hydrothermal activity or other unrest has been noted here, but it is assumed to be at least Pleistocene.

properties.name: Kinyo Seamount
properties.summary: Kinyo, one of the Shichiyo Seamounts, named for the seven days of the week ("Friday"), lies south of Sofugan volcano. No hydrothermal activity or other unrest has been noted here, but it is assumed to be at least Pleistocene.

properties.name: Ata Volcanic Complex
properties.summary: Volcanic features associated with 'Ata Island.

properties.name: Sangenges
properties.summary: Sangenges (also known as Puncak Ngenges) was mapped as Pleistocene to early Holocene by Garvin (2002, shown in Khant et al., 2013). Edifices immediately NE (Sesset) and SE (Batu Lanteh) are interpreted as Miocene-Pliocene features. This volcanic group forms the northern part of western Sumbawa, in the West Nusa Tenggara province of Indonesia. The 7-km-diameter caldera is open to the NNW.

properties.name: Tarowa
properties.summary: A geological map by Garvin (2002, shown in Khant et al., 2013) identifies this Tarowa as late Pliocene-early Pleistocene. This volcano is in the center of Sumbawa and includes an eroded caldera about 3.5 x 5 km, open to the SSW.

properties.name: Pesawaran-Ratai
properties.summary: Named for the two high points on the crater rim, the Pesawaran-Ratai edifice was probably a typical stratovolcanic cone that appears to have collapsed to the north, where the crater has breached. The volcano and surrounding area has been mapped as Quaternary on Indonesian geological maps (Mangga 1994, Suharno et al., 2015). Hot springs and geysers are present on the S flank (Suharno et al., 2015).

properties.name: Inacalari
properties.summary: The andesitic stratovolcano Cerro Inacalari is located about 25 km SE of Cerro del Azufre along the Chile-Bolivia border. Satellite imagery shows a small lake in the 400-m-diameter summit crater. It's age was estimated by Gonzales-Ferron (1995) as Pliocene-Pleistocene.

properties.name: Karasu Rift
properties.summary: The Quaternary basalts of the Karasu Rift form a belt covering an area 94 km long and 12-25 km wide (as revealed by boreholes) between Fevzipasa and north of Revhanli in the northern section of the rift (Rojay et al., 2001). Located near the far NE corner of the Mediterranean Sea, some of the lava field extends into Syria.

properties.name: Ceyhan-Osmaniye
properties.summary: The Ceyhan-Osmaniye volcanic field, as summarized by Gursoy et al. (2003), includes basaltic eruptions from about 20 vents (Yurtmen et al., 2000) dated between 0.61 +/- 0.10 and 2.25 +/- 0.78 Ma (Arger et al., 2000). Outcrops and volcanic units along the Karatas Osmaniye Fault Zone NE of the Gulf of Iskenderum  are described by a variety of names by different workers. Lava flows along the NW shoreline are identified by Gursoy et al.

properties.name: Mabda
properties.summary: The Mabda complex, also called Dubbi Alto, is composed of rhyolitic lava domes (Wiart and Oppenheimer, 2005). The north flank has been partially covered by lava flows from Dubbi volcano, but it's relationship to that edifice is unknown. Although the age is also unknown, it's location between two Holocene volcanoes makes a Pleistocene age likely.

properties.name: Lumut, Bukit
properties.summary: Located in south-central Sumatra overlooking the Semalako Plain, Bukit Lumut has a 2.1-km-diameter crater open to the north. It was mapped by Budiardjo et al. (2001) as the Pleistocene 0.893 Ma Lumut Andesite. Two small hills within that unit, one of which is name Bukit Pabus, consist of the slightly older Pabus Tuff (0.895 Ma). The Hululais volcano and geothermal are lies immediately to the SE.

properties.name: Tiga, Bukit
properties.summary: Located in south-central Sumatra SSE of the Semalako Plain, Bukit Tiga has a 1.3-km-diameter crater open to the SW. It was mapped by Budiardjo et al. (2001) as the Pleistocene 0.984 Ma Tiga Andesite. The Hululais volcano and geothermal are lies immediately to the N.

properties.name: Kawio Barat
properties.summary: The conical Kawio Barat submarine volcano sits just W of the Sangihe volcanic arc between Sulawesi Island in Indonesia and Mindanao Island in the Philippines. Satellite imagery showed submarine vents generating visible hydrothermal activity on the W side of the arc. A detailed survey was conducted in June 2010.

properties.name: North Kawio
properties.summary: The North Kawio volcano is a large primarily submarine edifice with multiple peaks, including the islands of Marore (Maru), Kawio, and Kamboreng.

properties.name: Toku
properties.summary: The island of Toku, about 20 km SE of Fonualei, is the emergent summit of a large submarine volcano. No eruptions have been recorded, but it is at the north end of the active Tofua Arc, making at least Pleistocene activity likely.

properties.name: Tofua Arc at 19.4°S
properties.summary: Bathymetry appears to show a large cone-like structure with a 5-km-diameter caldera located midway between Lateiki (25 km NNE) and Kao (25 km SSW). Although no reports of volcanism are known from this feature, it is directly along the active Tofua Volcanic Arc, and has likely erupted within the Pleistocene.

properties.name: Feinga Seamount
properties.summary: The bathymetry of this seamount shows a 4-km-diameter caldera open to the N, in which a dome appears to have grown. The edifice is located along the trend of the Tofua volcanic arc, about 43 km SSW of Tofua and 32 km NE of Fonuafo'ou (Falcon Island). Although no reports of volcanism are known from this location, it has likely erupted within the Pleistocene.

properties.name: Rahah-'Uwayrid, Harrat ar
properties.summary: Harrat ar Rahah-'Uwayrid is the northernmost of a series of Quaternary volcanic fields paralleling the Red Sea coast of Saudi Arabia, south of the city of Tabuk. The olivine basaltic field extends NW-SE about 240 km overall, and contains numerous scoria cones, tuff cones, and associated lava fields. The northern segments comprise Harrat ar Rahah, with an erosional divide where the field narrows to about 1 km at Matar.

properties.name: Te Kawa
properties.summary: The small (1.3 km diameter) crater-dominated Te Kawa cone and low Tokanui cone are located about 30 km S of the city of Hamilton in the Waikato region of North Island, New Zealand. They are the SE-most features of the Alexandra Volcanic Group, which includes an alignment of late Pliocene-early Pleistocene edifices, including the larger Kakepuku and Pirongia volcanoes, ending with Karioi more than 50 km NW on the Tasman Sea coast.

properties.name: Maungatautari
properties.summary: The Pleistocene Maungatautari stratovolcano is an andesitic-dacitic composite cone about 35 km SE of Hamilton on the North Island of New Zealand. Robertson (1983) reported a single K-Ar age of 1.8 ± 0.10 Ma, which Prentice et al. (2020) noted makes it contemporaneous with subduction-related volcanism of the nearby Alexandra Volcanics and the early Taupo Volcanic Zone.

properties.name: Tauranga Volcanic Centre
properties.summary: The late Pliocene to early Pleistocene Tauranga Volcanic Centre is located in the western Bay of Plenty region near the city of Tauranga, northwest of the Taupo Volcanic Zone. As defined by Pittari et al. (2021), this volcanic region comprises an eroded andesitic stratovolcano (Otawa Formation), approximately 17 rhyolite-rhyodacite lava dome complexes (Minden Rhyolite Subgroup), two ignimbrites (Waiteariki and Papamoa formations), and the small Matakana Fo…

properties.name: Haruman
properties.summary: The Quaternary Haruman lava dome is about 8 km ESE of Gunung Mandalawangi.

properties.name: Koil
properties.summary: Koil is a small island near the NW end of the Schouten Islands in the Bismarck volcanic arc between Vokeo and Vaia.

properties.name: Tofua Arc at 21.8°S
properties.summary: Informally designated as "Volcano 3" (R/V Sonne 167 survey).

properties.name: Tofua Arc at 22.0°S
properties.summary: Informally designated as "Volcano 4" (R/V Sonne 167 survey).

properties.name: Tofua Arc at 22.1°S
properties.summary: Informally designated as "Volcano 5a" (R/V Sonne 167 survey).

properties.name: Tofua Arc at 22.2°S
properties.summary: Informally designated as "Volcano 5b" (R/V Sonne 167 survey).

properties.name: Tofua Arc at 22.5°S
properties.summary: Informally designated as "Volcano 6e" (R/V Sonne 167 survey).

properties.name: Tofua Arc at 22.6°S
properties.summary: Informally designated as "Volcano 7" (R/V Sonne 167 survey).

properties.name: Tofua Arc at 22.8°S
properties.summary: Informally designated as "Volcano 8" (R/V Sonne 167 survey), and also known as Pelorus reef.

properties.name: Tofua Arc at 23.0°S
properties.summary: Informally designated as "Volcano 9" (R/V Sonne 167 survey).

properties.name: Kermadec Arc at 23.6°S
properties.summary: Informally designated as "Volcano 14" (R/V Sonne 167 survey).

properties.name: Kermadec Arc at 23.9°S
properties.summary: Informally designated as "Volcano 15" (R/V Sonne 167 survey).

properties.name: Kermadec Arc at 24.2°S
properties.summary: Informally designated as "Volcano 16" (R/V Sonne 167 survey).

properties.name: Kermadec Arc at 24.5°S
properties.summary: Informally designated as "Volcano 18 N" (R/V Sonne 167 survey).

properties.name: Kermadec Arc at 24.6°S
properties.summary: Informally designated as "Volcano 18 S" (R/V Sonne 167 survey). Caldera is about 6 km in diameter.

properties.name: Kermadec Arc at 25.2°S
properties.summary: Informally designated as "Volcano 20" (R/V Sonne 167 survey), or "Volcano V".

properties.name: Kermadec Arc at 25.4°S
properties.summary: Informally designated as "Volcano 21" (R/V Sonne 167 survey), or "Volcano U".

properties.name: Syoyo Ridge
properties.summary: Submarine volcanic ridge with eight peaks or seamounts along the East Mariana Ridge between Nikko and Fukujin. Unknown eruptive history.

properties.name: South Daikoku
properties.summary: Seamount about 50 km SE of Daikoku. Unknown eruptive history.

properties.name: Chamorro
properties.summary: Seamount about 35 km NW of Farallon de Pajaros. Unknown eruptive history.

properties.name: Cheref
properties.summary: Seamount about 30 km SSE of Asuncion Island. Eruption history is unknown.

properties.name: Poyo
properties.summary: Seamount about 50 km SSE of Asuncion Island. Eruption history is unknown.

properties.name: East Mata
properties.summary: East Mata is a submarine volcano in the northeastern Lau Basin at the northern end of the Tofua arc, about 200 km SW of Samoa and north of the historically active Curacoa submarine volcano. It was discovered during a November 2008 NOAA Vents Program expedition.

properties.name: Northern Matas
properties.summary: The Northern Matas volcanic ridges (Taha, Ua, Tolu, Fa, Nima, Ono, Fitu) are 900-1,300 m tall and variably elongate in ENE and E directions (Anderson et al., 2021).

properties.name: Niua Volcanic Complex
properties.summary: The Niua Volcanic Complex is a roughly rectangular area at the N end of the Tofua Arc, up to 25 km long and 13 km wide, that rises to depths of ~2,000 m above the seafloor; it is characterized by an irregular morphology, with smaller volcanic features that occur on the periphery of the larger edifices, and lava flows (Anderson et al., 2021).

properties.name: Tisa
properties.summary: Seamount about 45 km W of Tutuila Island. Koppers et al. (2011) reported an Ar-Ar date of 2.18 ± 0.03 Ma.

properties.name: Northeast Bank
properties.summary: Northeast Bank is a seamount about 45 km NW of Ofu-Olosega. Koppers et al. (2011) reported Ar-Ar dates of less than 1 Ma. The informal cruise designation of "Muli" has been present in the scientific literature since 1999, but should not be used as a common name.

properties.name: Soso
properties.summary: The Soso seamount is about 65 km NE of Tutuila Island. Koppers et al. (2011) reported Ar-Ar dates of 1.35-1.43 Ma.

properties.name: Tamai
properties.summary: The Tama'i seamount is about 65 km NNW of Tutuila Island. Koppers et al. (2011) reported Ar-Ar ages between 1.87 and 2.07 Ma.

properties.name: Tulaga
properties.summary: The Tulaga seamount is about 60 km ESE of Tutuila Island in the Samoan Islands. Koppers et al. (2011) report that Ar-Ar ages from samples dredged on the S flank are 0.79-1.07 Ma.

properties.name: Malutut
properties.summary: The Malutut seamount is the high point near the end of a submarine volcanic ridge that extends more than 40 km ESE from Tutuila Island in the Samoan Islands. Koppers et al. (2011) report that Ar-Ar ages from samples dredged on the SW flank are 1.04-1.48 Ma.

properties.name: Tofua Arc at 16.2°S
properties.summary: Seamount in the area between Niuatoputatu and Fonualei. Informally designated as "Volcano L" (R/V Southern Surveyor SS11/2004).

properties.name: Tofua Arc at 16.7°S
properties.summary: Seamount in the area between Niuatoputatu and Fonualei. Informally designated as "Volcano K" (R/V Southern Surveyor SS11/2004).

properties.name: Tofua Arc at 17.0°S
properties.summary: Seamount in the area between Niuatoputatu and Fonualei. Informally designated as "Volcano J North" (R/V Southern Surveyor SS11/2004).

properties.name: Tofua Arc at 17.2°S
properties.summary: Seamount in the area between Niuatoputatu and Fonualei. Informally designated as "Volcano J South" (R/V Southern Surveyor SS11/2004).

properties.name: Tofua Arc at 17.6°S
properties.summary: Seamount in the area between Niuatoputatu and Fonualei. Informally designated as "Volcano I" (R/V Southern Surveyor SS11/2004).

properties.name: Tofua Arc at 17.8°S
properties.summary: Seamount in the area between Niuatoputatu and Fonualei. Informally designated as "Volcano H" (R/V Southern Surveyor SS11/2004).

properties.name: Saray
properties.summary: Saray is a heavily eroded late Miocene-Quaternary volcano about 75 km WNW of Sahand. The small edifice forms Islami Island in Lake Urmia in NW Iran.

properties.name: Boku
properties.summary: Boku is a Pleistocene volcano that had a caldera-forming eruption around 830,000 years ago (Fontijn et al., 2018).

properties.name: Egrikuyu Monogenetic Field
properties.summary: The Egrikuyu Monogenetic Field is located in Central Anatolia S of Hasandag volcano and NE of the Karacadag edifice. As summarized by Uslular et al. (2021), the clustering of vents in this 28 x 38 km area follows a generally NE-SW in the west and mostly N-S to NW-SE in the east. Scoria cone alignments may indicate buried faults. There are a few basaltic maars in the region. Usulular et al.

properties.name: Telaga
properties.summary: The NE part of Tidore Island off the west coast of Halmahera contains an eroded volcanic edifice with the 2.1 × 2.2 km Telaga caldera (also called Sabale). The date of the caldera-forming eruption is unknown, but Faral et al. (2022) suggested that it occurred between 22,000 and 17,500 cal.

properties.name: Pomare
properties.summary: The Pomare stratovolcano (also known as Tavani Kutali or Nikalo) on Epi Island is immediately W and outside of the suggested submarine East Epi caldera. Epi Island is largely volcanic, with Mount Allombei on the west, Pomare on the east, and Tavani Ruro forming the SE peninsula. There are three subsidiary cones to the east.

properties.name: Tavani Ruro
properties.summary: The broad late-Pleistocene or Holocene Tavani Ruro volcano forms the SE peninsula of Epi Island, NW of Kuwae caldera.

properties.name: Tongoa
properties.summary: The volcanic island of Tongoa in Vanuatu is just south of Epi Island and the Kuwae caldera. The 4.5-km-diameter island includes multiple eroded volcanic cones, the most prominent being Tavani Hurata.

properties.name: Vanuatu Arc at 18.2°S
properties.summary: Submarine volcanic cone approximately halfway between Erromango and Efate islands in Vanuatu.

properties.name: Volsmar
properties.summary: The submarine Volsmar volcanic field lies near the southern end of the Vanuatu (or New Hebrides) Volcanic Arc, ~150 km SSE of Aneityum Island and about 60 km SSE of the Gemini-Oscostar cones. Bathymetric mapping has identified a large stratovolcano at the N end named Mariposa, and a slightly smaller volcano, Abeja, about 5 km SW; additional small cones extend 10-12 km further S.

properties.name: Balintang
properties.summary: The Balintang Islands are a group of seven small rocky islands in the middle of the Balintang Channel north of Luzon. The largest island is about 1,600 m long by 500 m wide, and reaches over 100 m above sea level. They are the summit of a large submarine edifice slightly smaller than the volcanic edifice under Babuyan Claro, 50 km SSW.

properties.name: Mabudis-Siayan
properties.summary: Submarine volcanic edifice with the islands of Mabudis, Maysanga, and Siayan representing the exposed summit area.

properties.name: Y'Ami-North
properties.summary: Submarine volcanic edifice with the islands of Y'Ami and North representing the exposed summit area.

properties.name: Addington Volcanic Field
properties.summary: The submarine Addington Volcanic Field is about 20 km offshore of Cape Addington on Prince of Wales Island, SW of Iphigenia Bay. This field is a possible source for late Pleistocene tephras deposited in southeast Alaska (Wilcox et al., 2019).

properties.name: Maclaren River Volcanic Field
properties.summary: As described by the Alaska Volcano Observatory, the Maclaren River Volcanic Field was first recognized by Brueske et al. (2023) and has been further characterized by Bearden (2023). The field, located east of the Maclaren River on either side of the Denali Highway, includes at least three monogenetic volcanoes that date from the last million years.

properties.name: Pandan
properties.summary: Small eroded Pleistocene cone in eastern Java about 40 km N of Wilis volcano and 10 km S of the main Kendeng Fault. As noted in a review by Alawiyah et al. (2022), there are several hot springs in the area, with a geothermal system hosted in a tuffaceous sandstone; the source of seismicity in the area is unclear.

properties.name: Tahulandang
properties.summary: Cone within a caldera breached to the north.

properties.name: Tamata
properties.summary: Largest of the three volcanic cones of central Siau Island just S of Karangetang. No age dates are known, but the distinct edifice with much less erosion relative to cones to the S suggests a Quaternary age.

properties.name: Makalehi
properties.summary: Back-arc island volcano W of the main Sangihe volcanic front, km W of Karangetang. The island is a 1.5-km-diameter caldera, breached to the SW, but with a 500-m-diameter post-caldera dome on the SW side of the caldera and a crater lake in the NE. The submarine edifice appears to be ~20 km in diameter. Identified as Quaternary by Hanyu et al. (2012).

properties.name: Kalama
properties.summary: The heavily eroded Kalama Island, just N of Mahengatang/Banua Wuhu and S of Sangihe Island, is the emergent summit of a larger submarine edifice. Hanyu et al, (2012) identified it as being part of the Quaternary volcanic front.

properties.name: Mamuya
properties.summary: Small stratovolcano outside the Dukono complex, 10 km NE of the summit along the coast. Previously an island, a lava flow during a major eruption of Dukono in 1550 CE filled in the strait, connecting Mamuya to Halmahera.

properties.name: Jumelles-Mwezi Volcanic Field
properties.summary: The submarine Jumelles Ridge and Mwezi province are lineaments of monogenic seamounts and domes approximately 60 km NE of Mayotte in the Comoros Islands. Rusquet at al. (2024) concluded that the Jumelles and Mwezi features represent a continuous zone of volcanic seamounts aligned along a N130-N135°E trend, with intermittent mafic activity from before 1.4 Ma until about 0.2 Ma.

properties.name: Gahinga
properties.summary: The Gahinga (or Mgahinga) stratovolcano is in the NE part of the Virunga Range, ~3.5 km E of Muhavura volcano across a broad saddle. The two volcanoes have produced basanitic-to-trachyandesitic lavas.

properties.name: Central Virunga Volcanic Field
properties.summary: Unofficially designated the Central Virunga Volcanic Field for this catalog, this volcanic ridge with many small cones extends ~12 km NE-SW along the Dr Congo-Rwanda border area between the Visoke and Sabinyo edifices. As noted by Pitcavage et al.

properties.name: Southern Virunga Volcanic Field
properties.summary: Unofficially designated as the Southern Virunga Volcanic Field for this catalog, this describes numerous cones within ~80 km2 on the lava plains of Rwanda SW of Karisimba volcano. As noted by Pitcavage et al. (2021), this is the second of three cinder cone fields in the Virunga area that "have produced primitive alkaline mafic lavas: (1) the Bufumbira volcanic field..., (2) Karisimbi primitive K-basanites (PKBs; Rogers et al., 1992) and (3) cinder cones lo…

properties.name: Tofua Arc at 19.9°S
properties.summary: Submarine cone seen in satellite bathymetry along the volcanic arc ~20 km SW of Tofua. No reports of eruptions are known.

properties.name: Bukendaban
properties.summary: Rhyolites dated to 1.5 Ma are mapped at the western end of the mostly snow-covered Bukendaban mountains (Wang et al., 2016) NE of Taiyang Lake in Tibet, just S of the Anyimaqen-Kunlun-Muztagh suture zone in the Songpan-Ganzi block. A feature ~75 km SE along the fault zone, described as the Kekexili caldera, was once thought to have been observed in eruption on a satellite photo in 1973; it was later determined to be a meteorological event (Kidd, 1990 pers.…

properties.name: Weixueshan
properties.summary: A group of small rhyolite cones, along the Anyimaqen-Kunlun-Muztagh suture zone between the Songpan-Ganzi and Central Kunlun blocks immediately N of a small 15-km-long mountain range, are mapped as "<1.0 Ma?" (Wang et al., 2016). A sample from this are was collected and analyzed by Jolivet et al.

properties.name: Laohukou
properties.summary: Shoshonitic cones 1-3 km in diameter, mostly covered by Quaternary sediments, are present in the Jingyu basin just NE of Jingyu Lake and SW of the Anyimaqen-Kunlun-Muztagh suture zone (Jolivet et al., 2003). Apatite fission track dating by Jolivet et al. (2003) gave 0.5 +/- 0.2 Ma, which were considered to correspond to crystallisation ages.

properties.name: Jindingshan
properties.summary: A small cone with a lava field covering ~65 km2 was identified in Wang et al. (2016) as non-adakitic trachyandesites in the 1.08-0.3 Ma age range. It is in the Central Kunlun Block, ~30 km N of the Anyimaqen-Kunlun-Muztagh suture zone with the Songpan-Ganzi block to the S.

properties.name: Southwest Pagan
properties.summary: Submarine volcanic edifice ~25 km SW of Pagan Island.

properties.name: West Guguan
properties.summary: Submarine volcanic edifice ~28 km WSW of Guguan Island.

properties.name: Northwest Zealandia
properties.summary: Submarine volcanic edifice ~18 km NW of Zealandia Bank.

properties.name: West Zealandia
properties.summary: Submarine volcanic edifice ~14 km W of Zealandia Bank.

properties.name: West Sarigan
properties.summary: Submarine volcanic edifice ~15 km WNW of Sarigan Island.

properties.name: West Diamante
properties.summary: Submarine volcanic edifice ~50 km SSW of Anatahan Island.

properties.name: West Saipan
properties.summary: Submarine volcanic edifice ~30 km NW of Saipan Island with a summit crater ~1.5 km in diameter.

properties.name: West Tinian
properties.summary: Submarine volcanic edifice ~15 km WNW of Tinian Island.

properties.name: West Rota
properties.summary: Submarine volcanic edifice ~35 km NW of Rota Island with an elongate 5 x 10 km summit caldera.

properties.name: Northwest Guam
properties.summary: Submarine volcanic edifice ~55 km WSW of Rota and ~45 km NW of Guam islands.
